session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Hey you! Happy new year, belatedly. How's January treating you so far?

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: Happy new year! It's been slow and grey, but I'm not complaining. I've mostly been hiding indoors with tea and podcasts.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Ooh, podcasts. Anything good? I'm in a rut and keep relistening to the same three shows.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: There's a history one I've been hooked on, about forgotten sea routes and the people who ran them. Sounds dry but the host is hilarious.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Okay, that actually sounds right up my street. Is it one of those where each episode stands alone, or do you have to start at the beginning?

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: You can jump in anywhere, honestly. I started in the middle and just worked backwards.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Perfect, I'll try one on my commute tomorrow. Have you watched anything good lately? I finally saw that quiet drama everyone was raving about last year.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: The one with the lighthouse keeper? I keep meaning to. Was it worth the hype?

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Mostly yes. It's very slow and the ending is a bit ambiguous, but the cinematography is gorgeous. I wanted to argue about it with someone afterwards.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: Ha, well save your arguments for me then, I'll watch it this weekend. I've been rewatching old comedies instead, which is peak comfort-zone behaviour.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: No shame in that, January is for comfort. Though all this gloom has me daydreaming about a holiday.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: Same! I keep flip-flopping between somewhere hot with nothing to do and somewhere with mountains and lots of walking.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Why not both? A week of lazing by water, then a few days of hiking somewhere cooler.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: Greedy, but I like it. Maybe we should both pick somewhere for later in the year and compare notes.

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Deal. I'll start collecting ideas and send you a shortlist. Nothing too ambitious, I just want a good view and a decent breakfast.

session_1.speaker: Teodor
session_1.text: That's honestly all I need from a trip too. Speak in a couple of weeks?

session_1.speaker: Sunniva
session_1.text: Definitely. Enjoy the lighthouse film, and tell me what you think of the ending!

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Hey you! How's the week been treating you so far?

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Pretty good actually, just busy. I finally watched that slow Korean film everyone kept recommending last weekend.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Oh nice, how was it? I started it once and fell asleep twenty minutes in.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Ha, fair, it does take its time. But the last half hour completely won me over, I was a bit of a mess by the end.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Okay, now I have to give it another go. Did you hear that Mikkel and Freja finally set a date for the wedding?

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: I did! Summer, right? I'm already trying to figure out how to get there from Aarhus without it taking all day.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Yeah, late June I think. We could probably travel together if the timing works out.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: That would be great, way less boring than going alone. Are you doing the speech thing, or is that someone else's job?

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: God, I hope not. Freja's brother is apparently already writing something, so I'm hoping I'm off the hook.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Smart. Stay quiet and nobody will think to ask you.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: That's the plan. Anyway, I've been listening to this podcast about old shipwrecks on my commute, and it's weirdly addictive.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Shipwrecks? That sounds oddly specific. Is it more history or more mystery?

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Bit of both. Each episode picks one wreck and goes through what went wrong, and the host has this very calm voice that makes everything sound worse somehow.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Haha, I love that. Send me the name, I need something new for my walks.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Will do, I'll message it over later tonight. Let me know what you think after a couple of episodes.

session_2.speaker: Sunniva
session_2.text: Deal. And you owe me a report on whether you ever finish that film.

session_2.speaker: Teodor
session_2.text: Fine, fine. Talk in a couple of weeks!

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Hey! Did you end up doing that trail you were talking about last time? The one with the ridge section?

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Yes, finally, on Saturday. The ridge was gorgeous but the last stretch was pure mud, my boots are still sitting on the porch drying out.

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Ha, classic. Was it busy up there or did you have it mostly to yourselves?

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Pretty quiet, we passed maybe four other groups the whole day. I'd go back in spring when it's drier.

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Spring sounds right. Honestly I'm just tired this week, the neighbour upstairs has been dragging furniture around at like midnight.

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Oh no, that's the worst. Have you said anything to them or are you still in the passive-aggressive sigh phase?

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Still in the sigh phase, I'm afraid. I keep telling myself I'll leave a polite note but then I never get around to writing it.

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Write the note. A friendly one works better than you'd think, people usually have no idea how much sound carries.

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: You're right, I'll do it tonight. Anyway, did you get the invitation to Marit's wedding? Ours came on Friday.

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Yes! It's such a lovely card, all handwritten. I can't believe she's actually getting married, I still picture her as the person who lost her shoes at that festival.

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Right, she walked home barefoot and was weirdly proud of it. Are you going to make a weekend of it or just do the day?

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: I was thinking of staying over, since it's a bit of a drive. Do you want to share a ride when it gets closer?

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Sure, that would be fun, and it means neither of us has to be the sober one driving back late.

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Exactly my thinking. We can sort out the details nearer the time, there's plenty of runway.

session_3.speaker: Sunniva
session_3.text: Perfect. I'm going to go write that note to the neighbour before I lose my nerve, talk soon!

session_3.speaker: Teodor
session_3.text: Good luck with it! Tell me how it goes, and I'll send you a photo of the muddy boots for the record.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: Hey you! How's the week looking so far? I feel like I haven't heard from you in ages.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Busy but good! I finally booked a checkup with Dr. Abernathy, so that's one thing ticked off the list.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: Look at you being responsible. I've been putting mine off for a year at least.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Honestly the big news is that I've moved. I'm in Dunedin now, still unpacking boxes.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: No way, you buried the lede! How's it been settling in? Are the boxes winning?

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: They're winning by a mile. Slowly getting there though, and I bought myself a new plant to make the place feel less bare. It's the monstera, and it already looks great by the window.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: Nice, those things get huge. Just don't let it take over the whole flat.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Ha, I'll hold it to a strict growth plan. Did you hear that Marit's wedding is finally locked in? I got the invite last week.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: I did! Mine came too. I'm already stressing about what to wear and whether I'll cry during the vows.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: You will, you always do. I'm just hoping the food is decent, because I have to be careful about the menu. I'm allergic to shellfish, so I need to flag it early.

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: Good call, better to tell them now than end up eating a sad bread roll. Speaking of food, I tried making that Thai curry from the video you sent and it was a disaster.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Oh no, what happened? Too spicy or just bland?

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: I somehow split the coconut milk and it turned into a weird oily soup. We ended up ordering pizza at nine o'clock.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Pizza is never a bad outcome, honestly. Did you get out at all this weekend, or was it all kitchen drama?

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: I did a hike on Sunday, the ridge trail with the long climb through the pines. Legs are still complaining but the view at the top was worth it.

session_4.speaker: Sunniva
session_4.text: Jealous! Send me a photo and I'll add it to my someday list. Talk again in a couple of weeks?

session_4.speaker: Teodor
session_4.text: Deal. And I'll send the photo tonight, if my legs let me reach my phone.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Hey you! How's the week treating you so far?

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Pretty gentle, actually. I finally watched that old black-and-white heist film you kept recommending, and I get the hype now.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Ha, told you! The ending where nobody says a word for five minutes is so good.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Right? Also, small life update: I switched dentists, I go to Dr. Marchetti now. The old place was a pain to get appointments at.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Nice, is the new one any better? I've been putting off my own checkup for ages.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: So far yes, and the waiting room doesn't smell like a hospital. Anyway, how did your cooking experiment go last weekend? You mentioned a recipe.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Oh no, don't remind me. I tried making a lemon tart and the filling never set, so we ate lemon soup in a pastry shell with spoons.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Honestly that sounds kind of delicious. Did you at least get the crust right?

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: The crust was perfect, which made it more insulting. I think I had the oven too cool.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Classic. Oh, and work is busy but fine, I'm at Halvorsen Freight these days, mostly spreadsheets and the occasional fire to put out.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Sounds like a decent mix. Is the commute okay?

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Wait, I need to correct myself, I said that wrong. It's not Halvorsen Freight, that was a slip on my part, I work for Mossgate Studio.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Ha, no worries, I was about to ask what a freight company wants with spreadsheets and fires. Studio makes more sense for you.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Yeah, much more me. Are you doing anything this weekend? I heard it's supposed to be properly sunny.

session_5.speaker: Teodor
session_5.text: Yes, forecast says clear skies both days, so I'm planning a long walk and maybe a picnic, with store-bought dessert this time.

session_5.speaker: Sunniva
session_5.text: Smart. I'll probably just sit outside with a coffee and do absolutely nothing. Talk in a couple of weeks?

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Hey you! Finally got a quiet evening, so I figured I'd check in. How's the week going?

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Hey! Pretty good, a bit tiring but good. I'm still getting used to everything being new, since I'm in Graz now.

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Right, that's still sinking in for me too, hearing you say it. Anyway, did you listen to that podcast I sent you?

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: I did! The one about the lighthouse keepers? I listened to two episodes on my walk yesterday, really hooked.

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Ha, yes, that one. The second episode is the best, wait until you get to the storm part.

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Don't spoil it! I'll save the rest for the weekend. Speaking of which, have you seen the forecast for Saturday?

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Yeah, supposed to be sunny and weirdly warm for March. I'm thinking of dragging a chair out onto the balcony and doing absolutely nothing.

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: That sounds perfect. I might go for a long walk if it holds up, then come home and cook something proper.

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Cooking, brave. I tried a recipe last Sunday and it went completely wrong. It was supposed to be a creamy mushroom pasta.

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Oh no, what happened?

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: I added the cream when the pan was too hot and it split into this grainy mess. Tasted fine, looked like soup with gravel in it.

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Ha! That's happened to me before, you have to take the pan off the heat first. Did you eat it anyway?

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Of course I ate it, I was starving. I just closed my eyes a bit.

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Fair enough. Oh, I almost forgot, I picked up a new plant this week, the pothos. It's already trailing over the edge of the shelf.

session_6.speaker: Teodor
session_6.text: Nice, those are supposed to be nearly impossible to kill, which is good news for the plant. Send me a photo!

session_6.speaker: Sunniva
session_6.text: Will do, once the light is better. Talk in a couple of weeks? Enjoy that balcony chair!

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Hey you! How was your week? I feel like I haven't talked to you in forever.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Hey! Pretty good, actually. I finally got out on that hiking trail I kept talking about, the one with the long ridge section.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Oh nice, the one with the waterfall at the halfway point? How was it?

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Gorgeous, but muddy. The road up to the trailhead is a bit rough too, my Mazda 3 scraped bottom twice and I winced both times.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Ha, I'd have winced too. Was it busy up there?

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Not at all, we had the ridge almost to ourselves. Got some great photos, I'll send you a couple later.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Please do. Okay, random question, are you going to Marit and Jonas's wedding next month? I still haven't decided what to wear.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Wait, I thought you had that nice navy suit? Yes, I'm going, I already RSVP'd. I'm mostly looking forward to the dancing.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: The navy suit is a little tight now, let's say I enjoyed the holidays too much. I might just rent something.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Renting is smart, honestly. And Marit said it's fairly relaxed, so you don't need to overthink it.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Good to know. Oh, and I have to tell you about my cooking disaster last weekend.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Uh oh. What did you make?

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: A fancy braised chicken recipe I found online. I misread the instructions and cranked the oven way too high, so the outside was basically charcoal and the inside was still raw.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Oh no, that's the worst combination! Did you salvage anything?

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: I scraped off the burnt bits, cut it up, and finished it in a pan. We ate it with a lot of rice and pretended it was intentional.

session_7.speaker: Sunniva
session_7.text: Honestly that sounds like a very Teodor solution. Next time just follow the recipe, you menace.

session_7.speaker: Teodor
session_7.text: Rude, but fair. Send me those hike photos, and let's talk again in a couple of weeks!

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Hey you! How's the week been treating you? Feels like it's flown by on my end.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: Pretty good, honestly. Quiet, which I needed. How about you?

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Same, mostly. Though I watched a film last night that I can't stop thinking about, that slow Icelandic one about the fisherman.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: Oh, the one with barely any dialogue? I've been meaning to see it. Was it worth the slow pace?

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Totally. The last twenty minutes got me. Just don't watch it when you're tired or you'll nod off by the second act.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: Ha, noted. Weekend viewing maybe. By the way, I picked up a new plant for the windowsill, the jade plant. It looks very pleased with itself already.

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Nice, those are supposed to be tough. Hard to kill, even for someone with my track record.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: That's exactly why I went for it. Low effort, high reward.

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Speaking of effort, my neighbour upstairs has taken up drumming. Or something that sounds like drumming. Last night at eleven.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: Eleven at night?! That's not okay. Have you said anything to them?

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Not yet. I left it at passive-aggressive sighing so far. Might knock on their door if it happens again.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: Passive-aggressive sighing never works, trust me. A friendly note usually does the trick, though.

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Fair point. A friendly note it is. Anyway, did you see the forecast for the weekend?

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: I did, it looks sunny on Saturday and then rain rolling in on Sunday. I'm planning to get outside as early as I can.

session_8.speaker: Teodor
session_8.text: Smart. I'll probably do a long walk Saturday and then hide indoors with tea on Sunday.

session_8.speaker: Sunniva
session_8.text: That sounds like a perfect weekend to me. Let me know how the drummer situation goes!

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Hey you! How was your weekend? It looked properly gorgeous out on Saturday.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: It was lovely, sunny the whole day and just warm enough to sit outside. Sunday turned grey and drizzly though, so I stayed in.

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Same here, Saturday was perfect and then Sunday just gave up. Did you do anything fun while it was nice?

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: Mostly lazy stuff, a long walk and a coffee in the sun. And on Sunday I finally started a series on Lumen, since I subscribe there and hadn't really used it much.

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Ha, the classic rainy day marathon. Any good so far?

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: Pretty good, slow burn but I'm hooked. I'll let you know if it holds up by the end.

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Please do, I'm always short of things to watch. Anyway, I've been daydreaming about a holiday lately.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: Ooh, tell me. Are we talking beach, city, or something more outdoorsy?

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Honestly I can't decide. Part of me wants somewhere hot and lazy, and part of me wants to be active and see something new.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: Why not mix it? A few days of exploring and then a few days doing absolutely nothing by the water.

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: That's actually a good plan. Speaking of being active, I did that hiking trail I mentioned, the one with the ridge at the top.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: Oh nice, how was it? I remember you said it was steep.

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Steep is an understatement, my legs were jelly for two days. But the view from the ridge was totally worth it.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: That sounds amazing. Was it busy, or did you mostly have it to yourself?

session_9.speaker: Teodor
session_9.text: Pretty quiet, we left early and had the first stretch almost empty. You'd like it, we should go together sometime.

session_9.speaker: Sunniva
session_9.text: I'd love that. Let's pick a good weekend once the weather settles a bit.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Hey you! How was your weekend? The weather was so odd here, sunny one minute and pouring the next.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Same here, honestly. I got caught in a downpour on Saturday, then sat outside in the sun on Sunday like nothing happened.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Classic. I ended up doing nothing but listening to a podcast on the sofa. It was about how old maps were made, weirdly gripping.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Ooh, send me the name of that one. I've been stuck on the same true crime show for weeks and I need a change.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Will do. It's a slow burn but the host has a lovely voice. Anyway, are we still on for book club this week?

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Yep, Thursday as usual. It's at The Dog-Eared Page, so I'll probably get there early and browse before everyone shows up.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Dangerous. You always leave with three more books than you planned.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Guilty. I'm running late a lot lately too, the Volvo V60 is great but parking near work is a nightmare. Anyway, have you read the book yet?

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: About two thirds of the way in. I'm not sure I like the ending I can see coming, but I'll reserve judgment.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: No spoilers! Oh, and I finally bought a new plant yesterday, the peace lily. I've wanted one for ages.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Nice, I hear those are pretty forgiving. Did it come with instructions or are you winging it?

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Winging it, obviously. I'm not as hopeless as I used to be, though. The jade plant is gone now, sadly, so I have a bare spot on the windowsill to fill.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Well, it's good to have a fresh start there. Speaking of fresh starts, I've been thinking about a holiday this summer.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Yes! Somewhere with a coastline, I think. I could happily sit by the water with a book for a week.

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: That sounds perfect to me. Maybe somewhere warm but not scorching, with good food and not too many crowds.

session_10.speaker: Sunniva
session_10.text: Agreed. Let's both look around and swap ideas next time we chat. Talk in a couple of weeks?

session_10.speaker: Teodor
session_10.text: Deal. See you Thursday at the club, and I'll send you that podcast name before then.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Hey you! Finally Friday. How's your week been?

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Long, but fine. I've been daydreaming about a proper holiday though, somewhere with a beach and absolutely no emails.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Ha, same. I keep flipping between a lazy beach week and something more active, like hiking in the mountains.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Mountains sound good until you remember the early starts. I'd probably pick the beach and pretend I'm adventurous by swimming a bit.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Honestly that's the right call. Oh, I have to tell you, I tried making a mushroom risotto last night and it turned into glue.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Glue? What happened?

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: I walked off to answer a call and came back to a solid brick of rice. The smoke alarm had opinions too.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Classic. I did something similar with a lemon cake last weekend, forgot the baking powder entirely and it came out like a flat pancake.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Did you eat it anyway?

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Obviously. With enough cream anything's edible. Speaking of boring grown-up stuff, I finally went through my bills and my phone plan is just $44 a month, which felt oddly satisfying.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Nice, that's a decent deal. I should probably check mine, I suspect I'm overpaying and just never look.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Do it, it takes ten minutes. I also made myself use the gym more, since I've got a membership at the Ironbridge gym and it was a waste sitting unused.

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Good for you. I can't even keep a gym habit going, I just walk a lot and call it fitness.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Walking counts! How's the neighbour situation, by the way? Still the late-night drilling?

session_11.speaker: Teodor
session_11.text: Worse. Now it's loud music until past midnight, and last night there was a bass thing going that rattled my shelves.

session_11.speaker: Sunniva
session_11.text: Ugh, that's miserable. Maybe leave a polite note first, and if that fails, earplugs and a very long beach holiday.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Hey you! How was your weekend? The weather was so odd here, sunny one hour and pouring the next.

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Same here, honestly. I got caught in a downpour on Saturday afternoon and then Sunday was perfect, not a cloud anywhere.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Typical. I wanted to get out on a trail but the forecast kept changing, so I stayed in and did nothing useful.

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Oh, speaking of trails, did you ever try that ridge loop you were talking about? The one with the lookout at the top?

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Not yet! I keep hearing it's steep for the first hour and then totally worth it. Maybe next weekend if it stays dry.

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Do it. Oh, quick thing before I forget, I gave you the wrong number for my phone plan ages ago. It's not $44, that was a mistake on my part, it's $27.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Ha, okay, noted. Good to have the record straight!

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Always. Anyway, are you going to Marit's wedding? I finally got the invitation in the mail.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Yes, I RSVP'd already. I'm a bit nervous about the speech situation though, I heard she asked a few people to say something.

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Oh no, I hope I'm not on that list. I'd just cry halfway through the first sentence.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: You and me both. I'll bring tissues for the whole table.

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Deal. Oh, and I treated myself on the way home from work last week and picked up the rubber plant. It's already looking pretty smug on the shelf.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: Smug is the right word for a rubber plant, they always look like they own the place. Does it get decent light there?

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Pretty good, by the window. We'll see if I manage to keep it going.

session_12.speaker: Teodor
session_12.text: You'll be fine. Right, I should get back to work, but let's talk again soon. Tell me how the wedding planning drama unfolds!

session_12.speaker: Sunniva
session_12.text: Will do. Enjoy that trail if you get out there, and take a rain jacket just in case!

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Hey you! Long time no chat. How's the weekend shaping up?

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Pretty lazy so far, which I'm not complaining about. How are you? Did you survive the wedding planning for Maja and Henrik?

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Ha, I'm not planning anything, I'm just a guest, but yes! It's next month and I still haven't figured out what to wear. Are you coming?

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Yes, I RSVP'd ages ago. I'll probably wear that green dress again, nobody remembers what I wore last time anyway.

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Smart. I tried to cook something fancy last night to practice for the buffet vibe and it was a disaster.

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Oh no, what happened?

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: I tried making a lemon risotto. Somehow it turned into a sticky, sour brick. I ended up eating toast over the sink.

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Classic. I did a similar thing with a banana bread last week, forgot the sugar completely. Tasted like sad bread.

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Sad bread is a real genre. Anyway, how was your week otherwise?

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Fine, I finally had my checkup, and I'm with Dr. Lindqvist now since my old one retired. She was really nice and quick about it.

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Good, I should book mine too, I keep putting it off. Did you watch anything good lately?

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Not really, I've been rewatching old stuff. You?

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: I saw that Icelandic film everyone's been raving about, the slow one with the sheep farmer. Honestly, I loved it, even though nothing really happens.

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: That sounds like my kind of film. I'll put it on this weekend. Also I have to tell you, I finally gave up on the monstera, it just got sadder and sadder and eventually I had to toss it.

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Aw, sorry to hear that. You'd had it for ages, hadn't you?

session_13.speaker: Sunniva
session_13.text: Yeah, a long while. My sister Ingrid says I should try something more forgiving, but I'm not ready yet.

session_13.speaker: Teodor
session_13.text: Fair enough, give it time. Anyway, let me know how the film is, and we'll compare outfit disasters before the wedding!

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I finally watched that old black-and-white thriller everyone keeps going on about. Took me two evenings because I kept falling asleep.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Ha, that's honestly the best way to watch anything slow. Was it worth it in the end?

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: Mostly yes. The last twenty minutes are really tense, and the ending caught me off guard. I'd say go for it if you have a quiet night free.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Adding it to the list. Oh, random update from me: I cancelled the Ironbridge gym membership. I was barely going and it felt silly to keep paying for it.

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: Fair enough, no point keeping something you don't use. Are you going to do something else to stay active instead?

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Walking, mostly. Which reminds me, I want to do a proper hike soon. Have you been on any good trails lately?

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: Yes! I did the ridge trail last Sunday. It's a long climb at the start but the view from the top is unreal, you can see for miles on a clear day.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Ooh, that sounds perfect. Is it very steep, or can a person who's been skipping the gym for months manage it?

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: You'll manage, just take it slow on the first stretch. Bring plenty of water though, there's no shade for a good while.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Noted. What's the weather supposed to do this weekend? I haven't looked yet.

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: I saw sunshine on Saturday and then clouds rolling in on Sunday, maybe a bit of rain in the evening. So Saturday would be the day for a hike.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Saturday it is, then. Do you fancy coming along? Could be fun to finally do a walk together.

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: I'd love to, as long as we start early. I'm useless in the afternoon heat and I get grumpy.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Early start, deal. I'll pack some snacks and you bring the water.

session_14.speaker: Teodor
session_14.text: Perfect plan. I'll message you Friday evening to confirm a time.

session_14.speaker: Sunniva
session_14.text: Sounds good. Talk then, and tell me if the film's ending ruins your sleep!

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I feel like I've been running on coffee and spite since Monday.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Barely. Did you hear the wedding is actually happening this Saturday? Our friend finally booked the barn and everything.

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: I heard! I still can't believe they're going with an outdoor ceremony in August. One thunderstorm and it's chaos.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Honestly that's half the fun. I'm just hoping the speeches are short, last wedding I went to, the best man talked for like forty minutes.

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Ha, I remember you telling me. Okay, so I need to confess something. I tried making a mushroom risotto last night and it turned into glue.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Glue? How do you even manage that with risotto?

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: I walked away to answer a call and came back to a solid brick of rice. I ended up eating toast over the sink like a student.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Classic. The only rule is you can't leave it alone, you have to stir the whole time. Anyway, are you coming to the next book club? It's Marginalia, same as always, and I'm hoping for good snacks this time.

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Ha, snacks are the real reason anyone shows up. Speaking of things going wrong, my upstairs neighbour has started practicing drums at night.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Drums? Actual drums, or like a little practice pad?

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Actual drums, I'm fairly sure. Last night it was a full solo at eleven, with cymbals and everything.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Oh no. Have you talked to them yet, or are you still in the passive-aggressive sigh phase?

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Deep in the sigh phase. I did leave a very polite note, which I'm now regretting because it sounded a bit too polite.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: Polite notes are underrated, they can't argue with you. Give it a few days and see if the drumming calms down.

session_15.speaker: Sunniva
session_15.text: Fair enough. What are you wearing to the wedding, by the way? Please tell me you're not recycling the same navy suit.

session_15.speaker: Teodor
session_15.text: I am absolutely recycling the navy suit. It's a classic, nobody's going to remember it!

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Hey you! Survived the week? I feel like August just evaporated.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Barely, ha. It's been one of those stretches where every day blurs into the next. How are you?

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Pretty good. I've been hooked on this podcast about lost expeditions, the kind where people vanish in the arctic and you just keep listening for 'one more episode'.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Oh that sounds exactly my thing. Is it narrated or more of an interview format?

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Narrated, with a guy who has this very calm voice that makes everything sound ominous. I fell asleep to it twice and then had to go back and find where I'd drifted off.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: That's the real test of a good podcast, honestly. Send me the name and I'll start it this weekend.

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Will do. Oh, and I tried making a mushroom risotto on Sunday and it was a disaster. I got impatient and cranked the heat, so the rice was crunchy in the middle and burnt on the bottom.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Oh no, risotto punishes impatience. You really do have to stand there stirring and adding stock little by little.

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: I know, I know. I ended up eating toast with cheese over the sink like a raccoon.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Honestly a respectable dinner. I've had worse ones that were supposedly planned.

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Did you get outside at all this month? I finally did a proper hike last weekend, the ridge trail with the long climb through the pines.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Nice! Was the view worth it? I always say the last twenty minutes of a climb are where you question every life choice.

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Completely worth it. The whole valley was lit up and there was hardly anyone else on the trail. My knees complained the entire way down though.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Knees always send the bill the next day. I'd love to try that trail sometime, it sounds like my kind of quiet.

session_16.speaker: Teodor
session_16.text: Let's do it in September when it's cooler. I'll bring snacks and you can bring the podcast recommendations you owe me.

session_16.speaker: Sunniva
session_16.text: Deal. I'll start yours tonight and report back, and you promise to skip the risotto.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Hey Kwame, how's your Monday going so far?

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Not bad. I finally got the new laptop set up over the weekend, and it's so much faster that I keep opening things just to watch them load.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Ha, nice. Mine is still the old one and it sounds like a small jet whenever I join a video call.

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Put in a request, they were pretty quick about mine. The migration of my dotfiles was the only annoying part.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Good to know. Did you try the coffee machine on the second floor yet? Someone apparently fixed it.

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: I did, and it's a big improvement. Before it tasted like warm cardboard, now it's actually drinkable, which is dangerous for my caffeine habits.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Dangerous for the rest of us too, there was a queue this morning. Anyway, anything I should know about before the week gets going?

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Just that I'm on the on-call rotation starting this week, so if I look a bit tired later, that's why.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Oh, good luck with that. I hope your phone stays quiet at night.

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Me too. Also, heads up, a new blocker bug was opened on the release this morning: the broken password reset.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. I'll make sure it gets looked at first thing tomorrow.

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Sounds good. I'm also fighting a flaky test that passes on my machine and then randomly fails when run with the rest of the suite.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Those are the worst. Is it a timing thing, or does it only fail in certain orders?

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Probably timing, but I haven't proven it yet. I'll poke at it after lunch with the new laptop, at least it'll fail faster now.

session_1.speaker: Liesel
session_1.text: Ha, small wins. Ping me if you want a second pair of eyes on it.

session_1.speaker: Kwame
session_1.text: Will do. Enjoy the rest of your Monday, and go grab some of that coffee before the queue gets long again.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Hey Kwame, how's your week going? Mine's been all meetings so far, I'm barely surviving.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Not bad at all. Yesterday's team lunch was the highlight, we finally tried that Ethiopian place near the office.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Oh nice, I heard about that. I had to skip it for a call, which still stings a little. Was it good?

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Really good. The injera was great and everyone shared off big platters, so it got pretty chatty. Even the quiet folks opened up.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: That's the best kind of lunch. Speaking of quiet folks, how's the new hire settling in? I've only caught glimpses of them in standup.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Doing well, I think. They've been asking a lot of questions, which I like. Yesterday they asked where a certain setup step was written down and I had to admit it lives mostly in my head.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Ha, that's the documentation debt talking. I keep meaning to block off time for it and then something else eats the calendar.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Same here. Honestly the newcomer is doing us a favor, every question they ask shows a gap we've stopped noticing.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: That's a good way to look at it. Maybe we have them jot down every spot where they got stuck and turn it into proper docs.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: I like that. Fresh eyes write better onboarding notes than any of us would, since we skip all the steps we do on autopilot.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Exactly. And it gives them an early win too, they get to leave a mark without touching anything risky.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Yeah, I'll suggest it at the start of next week. I'll pair with them for the first pass so it doesn't feel like homework.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Perfect. If it goes well we could try the same trick on the older pages nobody's touched in ages.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Some of those are fossils at this point. Half of them describe things we stopped doing ages ago.

session_2.speaker: Liesel
session_2.text: Ha, archaeology by wiki. Okay, I should run to my next meeting, but this was a nice break.

session_2.speaker: Kwame
session_2.text: Go, go. Talk in a couple of weeks, and say hi to the newcomer when you bump into them.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Hey Kwame, how's the week treating you? Feels like it's been a long one over here.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Pretty good actually, just quiet. The new person on the team started Monday and I've been showing them around the codebase.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Oh nice, how are they settling in? I only caught them briefly in the hallway on Tuesday.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Really well. Asks good questions, doesn't pretend to understand things when they don't. That's rarer than you'd think.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Love that. Honestly the best thing about onboarding someone is how it exposes everything we never wrote down.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Ha, yes. Half of what I explained on Monday was just stuff living in my head. I kept saying 'oh, it's sort of tribal knowledge' and then feeling guilty.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Documentation debt is real. We keep promising ourselves a cleanup sprint and then something shinier shows up.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: I started a rough getting-started page just from the questions they asked. Nothing polished, but it's already better than what we had.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: That's honestly the perfect way to do it. Write down what a real person actually needed, not what you imagine they'd need.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Exactly. If I'd tried to write it in the abstract I'd still be staring at an empty page.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Maybe we could all chip in a little each week. Even ten minutes after standup would add up.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: I'd be up for that. Small and regular beats a big heroic push that never happens.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Speaking of the new person, we should do a team lunch next week so they can meet everyone properly. Nothing fancy.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Yes please. There's that noodle place around the corner that's easy for a big group, and they do decent vegetarian stuff too.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Perfect, I'll float it in the team channel and see what day works for most people.

session_3.speaker: Kwame
session_3.text: Sounds good. Thursday tends to be the calmest day for me, but I'm flexible.

session_3.speaker: Liesel
session_3.text: Noted, I'll lean toward Thursday. Okay, I'll let you get back to it. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts!

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Hey Kwame, how's your week going? Feels like it's been one of those where everything takes twice as long.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Ha, yes, exactly that. I lost most of Tuesday chasing a flaky test that passed on my machine ten times in a row and then failed on the first run after lunch.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Ugh, the worst kind. Did you figure out what was going on?

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Pretty sure it's a timing thing, something racing with something else. I put a retry around it for now so it stops bothering everyone, but I don't love it.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: A retry is fine as a bandage as long as we don't forget it's there. Maybe leave a comment so future-you knows to come back to it?

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Already did, with a very passive-aggressive comment too. Anyway, are you coming to the team lunch on Friday?

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Yes! I voted for the noodle place. Last time we went somewhere with a ninety-minute wait and I nearly gave up.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Noodles get my vote too. I'll be there as long as nothing catches fire before noon.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Knock on wood. Oh, did your laptop upgrade ever come through? You were complaining about the fans a while back.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: It showed up on Wednesday! I spent half a day moving everything over, but the thing is silent now. Builds that used to make my desk vibrate don't even wake it up.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Nice, I'm a little jealous. Mine's still holding on, but the battery gives up around two in the afternoon.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: You should put in a request. IT was pretty quick about mine once I sent the right form.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Maybe I will. I keep telling myself I'll do it after the next release, which is basically never.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Ha, that's how I put mine off for a year. Just do it now and thank yourself later.

session_4.speaker: Liesel
session_4.text: Fine, you've convinced me. I'll fill it out after lunch today.

session_4.speaker: Kwame
session_4.text: Good. And save me a seat at the noodle place on Friday, I'll bring my quiet laptop as a trophy.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: Hey Kwame, got a few minutes? I wanted to ask how code review has been feeling lately, since a couple of people mentioned some comments getting a bit sharp.

session_5.speaker: Kwame
session_5.text: Sure, I've got time. I think it's mostly a tone thing, people write terse comments when they're rushed and it lands harder than intended.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: That makes sense. Do you have a rule of thumb you follow when you're leaving feedback?

session_5.speaker: Kwame
session_5.text: I try to phrase things as questions first, like 'what happens if this is null?' instead of 'this is wrong.' And I always say something good about the change before I pile on the nitpicks.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: I like that. Maybe we could put a short note about it in the contributor guide so newer folks see it from the start.

session_5.speaker: Kwame
session_5.text: Good idea. And speaking of the contributor guide, anyone cloning the code should know it lives in a repository named kestrel-core, since I keep seeing people ask in chat where to find it.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: Ha, yes, I'll make sure that's at the top of the guide. Which brings me to documentation, honestly we have so much debt there it's a bit embarrassing.

session_5.speaker: Kwame
session_5.text: Agreed. Half the setup steps in the wiki are out of date, and nobody wants to be the one to rewrite them.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: What if we carve out an hour at the end of each sprint just for docs? Nothing fancy, just fixing whatever tripped someone up that week.

session_5.speaker: Kwame
session_5.text: I'd be up for that. Small and regular beats a giant cleanup that never gets scheduled.

session_5.speaker: Liesel
session_5.text: Exactly. Oh, on a different note, did you end up watching that conference talk I sent you last week?

session_14.text: Hey Kwame, how's the week going? I saw you were at that conference talk on Tuesday, was it any good?

session_15.text: Just ask in the channel, people love to have opinions about food. It's the one topic where everyone's an expert.

session_15.text: Blunt how? Like rude, or just direct?

session_15.speaker: Liesel
session_15.text: Good. Also a quick 'nice work on the rest' never hurts. It costs nothing and people remember it.

session_15.text: Agreed. How's the newcomer settling in, by the way? I haven't had a proper chat with them since they started.

session_16.text: Ha, I'll hold you to that. Hey, did you catch any of the talks from that conference last week? I saw people posting about one on incremental refactoring.

session_16.text: That sounds painfully relevant. Our giant cleanup sprint has been 'next quarter' for as long as I can remember.

session_16.text: Right? Same energy as our documentation, honestly. We have a lot of pages that describe how things worked about a year ago.

session_16.text: Documentation debt is the one I feel guilty about most. Half the onboarding guide references steps nobody does anymore.

session_16.text: What if we tried the talk's approach there too? Whoever touches a part of the system fixes the related doc page in the same change, no separate project.

session_16.text: I like that. It's small enough that people might actually do it. I could add a line to the review checklist so it's a habit.

session_16.text: That would help a lot. Reviewers tend to follow whatever's on the checklist, so it'd stick better than a reminder in chat.

session_16.speaker: Liesel
session_16.text: Okay, I'll draft it this afternoon and send it around for feedback. Did the speaker say anything about measuring whether it works?

session_16.speaker: Kwame
session_16.text: Sort of. Just tracking how often people say 'the docs were wrong' in standup, which is a very unscientific but weirdly effective metric.

session_16.speaker: Liesel
session_16.text: I love that. Free, easy, and we'd know quickly if it's helping.

session_16.speaker: Kwame
session_16.text: Agreed. Anyway, I'm going to go refill that coffee machine before I forget. Want a cup?
