session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's off to a decent start. Did the office close for the long weekend like you thought it might?

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: It did, yes, we were shut Monday and I actually stayed away from my laptop for once. Feels like I'm paying for it today though, my inbox is a mess.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Ha, that's always the way. Is it busy generally at the moment?

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Properly busy, yes. Three other clients all want things turned around by Friday, so I'm juggling a bit. Nothing I can't handle, but I'll be a little slower replying than usual this week.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: No worries at all, I'm not in a rush this week. I'd rather you get it right than get it fast.

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Appreciate that. Speaking of getting it right, I spotted a silly typo in the latest draft when I was reading it over this morning.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Oh no, what was it? Something embarrassing?

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Just a doubled word and a company name with a letter missing. Harmless, but I'd have hated for it to go out like that.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Better you caught it than me. I read that thing three times and my eyes just slide over mistakes by now.

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Same here, honestly. I find the only trick is printing it out or changing the font, then the errors suddenly jump out.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: That's a good tip, I'll try that. Did you do anything nice with your day off, by the way?

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Mostly cooked and watched a film I'd been putting off for ages. Very low key, which was exactly what I needed.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Sounds perfect. We were closed too, so I caught up on sleep and not much else.

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Sleep is underrated. Anyway, I'll send over the corrected draft once I've fixed that typo and had another proper read.

session_1.speaker: Ottilie
session_1.text: Great, thanks. No hurry, like I said.

session_1.speaker: Rafiq
session_1.text: Will do. Speak in a couple of weeks, and shout if anything comes up before then.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Morning Rafiq! I read through the latest draft over the weekend and spotted a typo on page 4, "supplyer" with a y. Tiny thing but it jumped out at me.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Ha, good catch. I'll fix that in the next turn of the document, I'm amazed it survived three read-throughs.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Honestly I only noticed because I was reading it on the train with nothing else to do.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Whatever works! Anyway, I wanted to tell you where we landed with the other side on the cap. They've agreed the liability cap is $5 million, so that's settled from my point of view.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Oh nice, that's a relief. I wasn't sure they'd move at all on that one.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: They took a while to come round, but we got there. Speaking of which, they're being painfully slow to reply at the moment. I sent my last email nine days ago and only got an answer this morning.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Nine days? That's ridiculous. Do you think they're doing it on purpose to wear us down?

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Hard to say. Could be tactics, could just be that their people are swamped. I'd lean towards disorganised rather than devious.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Fair enough. Oh, one thing I meant to mention, when I spoke to our ops team they raised a new point they want covered, the delivery penalties. They think we need something clear in there.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Let me think about how best to frame that and I'll come back to you with a suggestion.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Sounds good, no rush. I know you've got a lot on.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Not too bad this week, though the office is closed on Friday for the holiday, so I'll be offline that day.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Lucky you, a long weekend! I think we're open but half the team has booked it off anyway.

session_2.speaker: Rafiq
session_2.text: Ha, classic. I'll aim to get the corrected draft over to you before I log off Thursday, typo included.

session_2.speaker: Ottilie
session_2.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks!

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your weekend was decent. I spent most of Friday walking a visitor round the plant and my feet are still complaining.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Ha, mine was quiet, thanks. How did the visit go? Anyone get lost among the machines?

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Nobody got lost, but the guy kept stopping to ask about every single conveyor. Took us twice as long as planned.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Classic. At least he was interested. Better than someone checking their phone the whole time.

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: True. Anyway, on the agreement, I want to nail one thing down so we stop going round in circles: the minimum annual order volume is 55,000 units. That's settled on our side.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Understood, I'll treat that as fixed and work from it in the next draft.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Speaking of the draft, I found a typo in the version I sent you last week. Someone's name was spelled two different ways in the same paragraph, which is embarrassing.

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Ha, I didn't even notice. I probably read it too fast on the train.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: No harm done, I've already corrected it. I'll send a clean copy later today.

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Great. Oh, and something new popped up on their side this week: the insurance certificates. They've started asking about them and I wasn't expecting that.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Okay, thanks for flagging it. Can you forward whatever they sent you so I can see exactly what they're asking for?

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Will do this afternoon. Honestly, I'd have sent it sooner but it took them ages to even get back to me about it.

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: Yes, they've been slow with me too. I sent a short question on Tuesday and I'm still waiting.

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Typical. Do you want me to nudge them from my end, or would that just annoy them?

session_3.speaker: Rafiq
session_3.text: A friendly nudge from you can't hurt. I'll chase on my side tomorrow if we've heard nothing.

session_3.speaker: Ottilie
session_3.text: Sounds good. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they surprise us and actually reply.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's going alright. I was at the plant most of yesterday walking some visitors round, and my feet are still complaining.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Ha, sounds like a long day. Did the visit go well, or was it one of those where everything breaks the minute guests arrive?

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Pretty smooth, actually. One of the machines made a horrible noise right as we passed it, but nobody seemed to mind.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Classic. Machines always know when there's an audience.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Anyway, on the deal itself, a new one came up this week that I wanted to flag. The other side raised the indemnity wording and said they want to rework it.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Okay, thanks for telling me. I'll take a look at what they've sent and think about how we want to respond.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Great. And speaking of the other side, they take forever to get back to us. I sent a quick question on Monday and I'm still waiting.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Yes, I've noticed the same. Their replies tend to trickle in two or three days late, so I've stopped expecting anything quick.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: At least there's some good news too. We finally got the delivery penalties settled, which feels like a weight off.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: That's a relief, that one was dragging on. I'll update the draft so it reflects what you agreed.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Perfect. By the way, I spotted a typo in the latest draft you sent. There's a word in one clause that's missing a letter and it changes the meaning a bit.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Oh no, thanks for catching that. Which clause was it? I'd rather fix it before it goes any further.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: It's in the middle section, I'll send you a screenshot so you can find it quickly.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Please do. I'll correct it and send round a clean version in the next day or so.

session_4.speaker: Ottilie
session_4.text: Sounds good. Thanks Rafiq, talk in a couple of weeks unless something comes up.

session_4.speaker: Rafiq
session_4.text: Will do. Enjoy the rest of your week, and give your feet a rest!

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is going okay. Are you around the Easter break at all?

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: Hi Ottilie, doing well thanks. The office closes from Thursday through the Monday after, so I'll be offline for a few days. I'll flag anything urgent before I go.

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Fair enough, you deserve the rest. Our plant shuts for that stretch too, so it works out nicely.

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: Good. Speaking of the plant, didn't you have a visit lined up there recently?

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Yes, the Marlow team came by last week and walked the whole floor. They seemed genuinely impressed with the line, and the engineers got along well.

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: That's encouraging. Site visits like that tend to smooth things along. Did they ask many questions?

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Loads, mostly practical stuff. Oh, and while I remember, we've settled that deliveries go to Bilbao, so please make sure that's what the draft says.

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: Noted, I'll check the draft against that and correct it if needed. Thanks for catching it.

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: No problem. Honestly the bigger frustration is how slow they are to reply. I sent a question ten days ago and heard nothing until yesterday.

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: Yes, I've noticed the same on my end. Their side tends to go quiet for a week and then fire back several answers at once.

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Exactly that. Is it worth nudging them a bit more firmly, or would that just annoy them?

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: A polite but firm nudge with a clear deadline usually works. I can draft something short for you to send under your name if you like.

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Please do. Also, one thing I wanted to make sure we're aligned on: the agreement includes an exclusivity clause, right?

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: Understood, I'll keep that in view as I go through the draft. I'll send you the nudge email tomorrow so you can have it out before the break.

session_5.speaker: Ottilie
session_5.text: Perfect, thank you. Enjoy the long weekend when it comes.

session_5.speaker: Rafiq
session_5.text: You too, Ottilie. Talk in a couple of weeks.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is going okay. I just got back from walking the plant floor with some visitors and my feet are done.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Hi Ottilie! Mine's been a bit of a blur, honestly. How did the visit go?

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: Pretty well. The guys were impressed with the new packing line, and nobody tripped over anything, which I count as a win.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Ha, low bar but a good one. I always worry when I visit a factory that I'll wander into the wrong yellow line.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: You'd be fine, we'd give you a hi-vis vest and a stern look. Anyway, while I have you, I should mention that Ms. Oyelaran is the one who'll be signing for Marlow Ltd.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Good to know, thanks for passing that along. I'll keep that in mind as we go.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: No problem. Have you heard anything back from their side lately? I feel like I've been waiting forever.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Nothing yet, sadly. They're not exactly speedy, every reply seems to take them days.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: It's maddening. I send one email and then just stare at my inbox like it owes me money.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Ha, I know that feeling. I've started batching my chasers so I'm not pestering them every other day.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: Smart. How's your workload, by the way? You sound like you're juggling a lot.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: It's been heavy. Three other matters landed on my desk at once this week, so I've been living on coffee.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: Oof, please don't burn out on me. I need you sharp.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Ha, I'll do my best. I'm planning a quiet weekend to recover, maybe just a long walk and a lot of nothing.

session_6.speaker: Ottilie
session_6.text: That sounds perfect. I might do the same once this plant visit stuff settles down.

session_6.speaker: Rafiq
session_6.text: Sounds like a plan. Talk again in a couple of weeks, and enjoy putting your feet up tonight.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Morning Ottilie. How did the visit to your plant go last week? You said you had the whole afternoon booked.

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Morning! It went well, though it ran long. I ended up walking the floor with the production team for nearly four hours and my feet are still complaining.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Ha, that's the price of actually going and looking. Did anything useful come out of it?

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Quite a bit. The line supervisor showed me how they handle changeovers, which I'd never really understood from the reports. Oh, and speaking of the deal, Marlow came back to us yesterday and raised something new: the tooling ownership.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Right, I wondered if that would surface. Can you forward me their email so I can read their exact wording before we talk about it?

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Sure, I'll send it over after we're done chatting. It was only a short paragraph, nothing too elaborate.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Good. Short paragraphs sometimes hide the most inconvenient assumptions, so I'll read it carefully. By the way, I spotted a typo in the latest draft, a clause number that points to the wrong section.

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Oh no, did I miss that when I read it? I went through it twice on the train.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Don't worry, it's an easy one to miss. It's a cross-reference that didn't update when we reshuffled the sections. I've already fixed it in my copy.

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Thank you. Please send me the corrected version so I'm not working from the old one.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Will do, it'll be in your inbox this afternoon. Shall we pencil in the next call? I'm fairly open the week after next.

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Let me check my diary. I'm travelling for the first half of that week, but Thursday looks free.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Thursday works for me. Mid-morning, say ten thirty, so you're not rushing from an early train?

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Ten thirty is perfect. I'll put it in my calendar now.

session_7.speaker: Rafiq
session_7.text: Great, I'll send an invite too. Have a good rest of your Monday, and rest those feet.

session_7.speaker: Ottilie
session_7.text: Ha, I will. Speak soon, Rafiq.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: Hi Rafiq, did you get a chance to look at the latest draft? I spotted a typo on the second page, our company name has an extra letter in it.

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Ha, good catch. I read that page three times and still missed it. I'll fix it in the next version.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: No worries, it's the sort of thing you only see when you're not staring at it all day. How's your week going, you sound busy?

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Honestly it's been a bit of a crush. Three other matters landed on my desk at once, so I'm working through evenings. But yours is still near the top of the pile.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: I appreciate that. Still waiting on Marlow to get back to us on the last round, by the way. I sent a nudge to my contact there, and since the cargo is going into Felixstowe now I'm keen to get things moving, but nothing yet.

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Yes, they've been slow every time. I chased their side again on Monday and got an automatic out-of-office back.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: Typical. Do you think they're doing it on purpose, to wear us down?

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Possibly, though I think it's more likely just internal sign-off dragging. Big companies tend to move at the pace of their slowest approver.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: That makes sense. I'd rather they were slow than difficult, I suppose.

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Fair point. Slow is annoying but manageable. I'll send them a polite reminder tomorrow and copy you in.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: Perfect, thank you. Do you want me to proofread the next draft before it goes out? A second pair of eyes might help with the typos.

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: That would actually be really useful, given how my eyes are feeling this week. I'll send it over once I've made the fixes.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: Sounds good. Try to get some rest in between all those matters, won't you?

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: I'll do my best. A long weekend is coming up and I'm planning to do absolutely nothing.

session_8.speaker: Ottilie
session_8.text: Sounds lovely. Speak in a couple of weeks, or sooner if Marlow finally wakes up.

session_8.speaker: Rafiq
session_8.text: Will do. Talk soon, Ottilie.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week is starting okay. Are you buried at the moment?

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: Pretty buried, honestly, but nothing I can't handle. Mondays are always a pile-up of emails.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: I hear you. One thing I wanted to pass on: the person signing for Marlow Ltd is now Ms. Devereux, so it's no longer the person we'd been expecting.

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know. I'll update the signature block on my side.

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: I also wanted to tell you that the liability cap has moved to $1.2 million after the latest round of comments.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Got it, that's useful to know. Thanks for chasing that down.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Oh, and the agreement is governed by Ontario law, just so you have it for the cover page.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Wait, sorry, I need to take that back. It's not Ontario law, that was a mistake on my part. It's English law.

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: Good catch, glad you flagged it straight away. I'll make sure the draft reflects that.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Thanks. Now, for the printing, do you want me to print the signature pages at the office or would you rather send them over?

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: I'll send a PDF set and you can print on your end. Just sign in blue ink if you can, it photocopies better.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Easy enough. Do I need a witness, or can I just sign and scan it back to you?

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: Just sign and scan for now, and we'll swap the originals by courier later.

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Perfect. By the way, Marlow's lawyers are the firm Hartwell Breck, in case you want to loop them in on the signing logistics.

session_9.speaker: Rafiq
session_9.text: Will do, I'll reach out to them this week. When should we have our next call?

session_9.speaker: Ottilie
session_9.text: Two weeks from now works for me, mornings are best. Just send an invite and I'll accept it.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Hi Rafiq, got a minute? I was reading through the latest draft last night and spotted a typo in the definitions section.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Of course. Which one? I read that draft twice and clearly my eyes glazed over somewhere.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: One of the defined terms is spelled two different ways, once with a double letter and once without. Tiny thing, but it jumped out at me.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Good catch, thank you. I'll fix it and check whether the same slip crept in anywhere else before we send the next version over.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Speaking of sending things over, have they come back to you on anything yet? I haven't heard a peep.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Not a word since last week. They're honestly the slowest people I've dealt with this year, every reply takes days.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: That's what I figured. I sent them a quick note myself on Monday and got nothing back, not even an acknowledgement.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Classic. I'll nudge them again tomorrow morning, politely, and see if that shakes anything loose.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Thanks. Oh, one thing I meant to mention while I think of it: there's an escrow arrangement for the tooling costs, so that's something to keep in mind when you're reading the drafts.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Noted, I'll keep that in view as I go through. How are you doing otherwise, is the rest of your week manageable?

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Pretty hectic but fine. What about you, are you drowning in work at the moment?

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: A bit, yes. I've got three other matters all landing deadlines at once, so I'm living on coffee and calendar reminders.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Ouch. Please don't burn out on my account, I'd rather you take an extra day than send me something rushed.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Ha, I appreciate that. Don't worry, yours gets proper attention, it's just the evenings that suffer.

session_10.speaker: Ottilie
session_10.text: Fair enough. Let's catch up again in a couple of weeks unless something moves sooner.

session_10.speaker: Rafiq
session_10.text: Sounds good. I'll fix that typo and ping you the moment I hear anything back.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Hi Ottilie, good to hear from you. How was the visit to the plant?

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Pretty good actually. Walked the whole line with the floor manager and the new packing area is finally running.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Nice, that must be a relief after all the delays. Did you get any time to look at the draft I sent?

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: I did, on the train back. Quick check, the payment term in there is 90 days, right? That's what I remember us landing on.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Yes, that's what the draft says. I'll leave it as is.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Good. Oh, and one thing from their side came in yesterday: they want to raise the audit rights, so that's a fresh item on the table.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Hm, that's a bit annoying this late in the process. I'll want to see exactly what they're asking for before I react.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Same here. On the bright side, we did finally close out the tooling ownership, so that one's off the list.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Great, that was a sticky one, so I'm glad it's done. One less thing to fight over.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: How's your workload? You sounded swamped last time.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Still swamped, honestly. I've got three other deals closing this month, so I'm living on coffee.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Ha, sorry to add to the pile. The other side is taking forever to reply, which doesn't help either.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Tell me about it. I sent them a note a week ago and got an out-of-office, then silence.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Classic. Anyway, I keep reminding myself the whole thing is just a supply deal for ceramic bearings, it shouldn't be this painful.

session_11.speaker: Rafiq
session_11.text: Ha, they never are as simple as they should be. I'll chase them again tomorrow and send you a summary once they answer.

session_11.speaker: Ottilie
session_11.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Morning Ottilie. Still no word from the other side since Monday, which is becoming typical. I swear they reply in geological time.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Ha, tell me about it. I stopped holding my breath weeks ago.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Wise. One thing did come through though: who signs for Marlow Ltd has changed and it's now Mr. Nakagawa. I'll update the signature block on our side.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Okay, good to know. Do I need to do anything on my end for that?

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Nothing at all for now, I'll just make sure the draft reflects it. How did the plant visit go, by the way? You mentioned a tour was coming up.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: It was good, actually. Walked the whole floor with a couple of their engineers and the place was spotless. Noisy though, my ears were ringing by lunchtime.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Sounds like a proper working site. Did you get to see the production line running?

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Yes, a full shift in progress. It was reassuring to see it up close rather than just in photos.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Always worth it. Oh, and I found a typo in the latest draft, a clause number was referenced wrong in the definitions section. Small thing, but I've flagged it.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Good catch. Speaking of mistakes, I need to correct something I told you earlier. The payment term in the agreement is not 90 days, that was my error. It is 45 days.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Thanks for flagging that, glad you caught it before it went anywhere. I'll make sure everything on my side matches.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Sorry about the mix-up. I think I had an old note in front of me.

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: No harm done, it happens. I'd rather you tell me now than after a draft goes out.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Fair enough. Anything else you need from me this week?

session_12.speaker: Rafiq
session_12.text: Not really. I'll send over the corrected draft once I've fixed that typo, and then we wait for the other side to wake up.

session_12.speaker: Ottilie
session_12.text: Perfect. Talk in a couple of weeks, then. Enjoy the weekend!

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Hi Rafiq, any word from Marlow's side? I've been refreshing my inbox like a maniac.

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Nothing yet. They took four days to answer a one-line question last week, so I'm not holding my breath.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Ugh, they're so slow. Though I did hear something useful through the grapevine: the person signing for Marlow Ltd is now Ms. Winterbourne.

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Good to know, thanks. I'll make sure the signature block gets updated so we don't have to redo pages later.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Perfect. Oh, and the liability cap is now $3.5 million, in case that hadn't reached you yet.

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Noted, I'll fold that into the next draft. Speaking of drafts, I spotted a typo in the one I sent you on Monday. A clause number was repeated twice.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Ha, I read that thing twice and missed it. Which section was it?

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Near the end, in the boilerplate. Harmless, but I've already fixed it in the working copy.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Good catch. One more thing before I forget: the escrow arrangement was dropped.

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Understood, I'll strip that out of the draft as well. Cleaner that way.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Now, signing logistics. Do you want me to print everything and sign in ink, or is a scanned signature fine?

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Wet ink is safest for the main agreement, but scans are fine for the schedules. I can courier you the pages if you don't have a printer handy.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: I do have a printer, but it jams constantly. A courier sounds less stressful, honestly.

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Done, I'll arrange it once the final version is ready. Use a blue pen so it's obvious which is the original.

session_13.speaker: Ottilie
session_13.text: Blue pen, got it. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if Marlow ever wakes up!

session_13.speaker: Rafiq
session_13.text: Ha, I'll let you know the second they reply. Talk soon!

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: Morning Rafiq! Hope your Saturday isn't entirely swallowed by work.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: Ha, mostly swallowed, but I've got coffee and a quiet office, so I can't complain.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: I was thinking the other day about that old deal we did together, the warehouse lease one. Remember how the landlord kept changing his mind about the car park?

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: How could I forget. He rang me at 9pm on a Sunday about a single parking bay. I still bring it up as the gold standard of pointless drama.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: You handled it so calmly though. I'd have lost it.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: Years of practice at looking calm while screaming inwardly. Speaking of which, I should say that our firm understanding is that the minimum annual order volume is 70,000 units, and that's what it's been all along.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: Anyway, are you drowning at the moment? You sounded exhausted on the last call.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: A bit, yes. Three matters landed on my desk at once and one of them is a monster. But it's the good kind of busy, mostly.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: Make sure you actually take a break at some point. Don't make me send you a wellness reminder.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: Noted. I'm taking next Friday afternoon off, I swear. Not that anyone believes me.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: We should have you out to the plant sometime, by the way. You've never actually seen the production floor.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: I'd love that, honestly. I've only ever seen it in photos. Is it as noisy as everyone says?

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: Louder. We hand out ear defenders at the door and the team has a whole system of hand signals.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: Now I really want to come. I'll bring a hard hat and pretend I know what I'm looking at.

session_14.speaker: Ottilie
session_14.text: Deal. Maybe in a few weeks when things calm down. I'll check the calendar and message you.

session_14.speaker: Rafiq
session_14.text: Perfect. Enjoy what's left of your weekend, Ottilie.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Hi Rafiq, hope your week's not too manic. Feels like I haven't heard from you in ages, though I know that's not true.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Ha, it's been a bit of a slog, honestly. I've got about four things all due before the end of the week and my inbox looks like a crime scene.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Oof, sorry to add to the pile. I'll keep this short then.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: No no, you're fine. Talking to you is the nice part of my day compared to some of the others.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Flattery. Are you at least getting a break soon? I seem to remember the office shuts for a bit.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Yes, we're closed on the Monday of the long weekend, so I'll be offline that day. I'm planning to do absolutely nothing and maybe fix the shed door.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: That sounds perfect. I might do the same, the shed is optional.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Strongly recommend the nothing part. The shed door is just guilt.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Speaking of waiting around, have you heard anything back from the other side lately?

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Not yet. They took nearly a week to answer my last email, and when they did it was two lines saying they'd 'revert shortly'.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Shortly is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Right? I've stopped checking for replies every hour. It's better for my blood pressure.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Wise. I'd rather you spend that energy on the shed door anyway.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Ha, don't tempt me. I'll nudge them again on Friday if we haven't heard anything.

session_15.speaker: Ottilie
session_15.text: Sounds good. Thanks for being so patient with all this.

session_15.speaker: Rafiq
session_15.text: Anytime. Talk in a couple of weeks, and enjoy the long weekend!

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Morning Rafiq. Still nothing back from Marlow, and it's been over a week now. Is it just me or are they getting slower?

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: It's not just you. They seem to take their time on everything lately, and a reply usually lands on a Friday afternoon when nobody can do anything with it.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Ha, classic. I keep refreshing my inbox like it's going to change anything.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: I did the same thing yesterday. Honestly I should stop, it's bad for my blood pressure.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Speaking of which, how's your workload? You sounded swamped last time we spoke.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: Still pretty heavy. I've got three other clients all wanting things by the end of the month, so my desk looks like a paper explosion.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Sorry to add to the pile. I'll try to keep my emails short.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: Oh, you're no trouble at all. You're one of the easier ones, you actually answer when I ask a question.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Low bar, but I'll take the compliment. By the way, I had some visitors at the plant on Thursday and walked them round the whole floor.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: Oh nice, how did that go? I've never actually seen a plant like yours in person.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: You should come. It's loud and a bit hot, but people always find it fascinating once they see the machines running.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: I'd love that, genuinely. Maybe once things calm down a bit I can take a morning and drive out.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Deal. I'll even find you a hard hat that fits, though I can't promise the ear defenders are comfortable.

session_16.speaker: Rafiq
session_16.text: I'll risk it. Right, I'd better get back to the paper explosion, but I'll let you know the second Marlow surfaces.

session_16.speaker: Ottilie
session_16.text: Perfect, thanks Rafiq. Talk in a couple of weeks, or sooner if they wake up.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Hello Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just doing our regular check-in, how are you keeping?

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: Hello Emeka! Not too bad at all, thanks. A bit tired this week but I think that's just the weather.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Understandable, it's been grey and damp for ages. Have you been getting out for any walks at all?

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: A few short ones round the block when it's dry. My granddaughter came over on Saturday and dragged me to the park, so that counted for a good long one.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Ha, grandchildren are the best personal trainers. How old is she now?

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: She's seven going on seventeen. She wanted to show me how she can do cartwheels, and I told her my cartwheeling days are well behind me.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Quite right too! And how has the eating been lately, in general? Still keeping to regular meals?

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: Mostly, yes. I'm having more soups and stews this time of year, and I try not to snack in the evenings, though the biscuit tin does call to me now and then.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Soups and stews are a good choice in winter, nice and filling. The odd biscuit isn't the end of the world, just keep an eye on it.

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: That's what I tell myself! Oh, by the way, I was filling in a form at my neighbour's and realised I wasn't sure you had it down right. The doctor I'm under is Dr. Grieve.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Thanks for mentioning that, I'll make sure our notes are all in order. Better to double check these things.

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: Grand. Now, is the flu still going round? Half the women at my church group have been coughing and spluttering.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: It's been a busy season, yes, lots of colds and flu about. Wash your hands well, and if you start feeling feverish or achy, give us a ring early.

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: I will. I'm keeping my distance from anyone who sounds croaky. My granddaughter had the sniffles last week though, so I'm hoping I escaped.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Fingers crossed. Any other worries you want to raise before I let you go?

session_1.speaker: Bronagh
session_1.text: No, I think that's everything. Thanks for ringing, Emeka, it's nice to have someone checking in.

session_1.speaker: Emeka
session_1.text: Anytime, Bronagh. I'll be in touch again in a couple of weeks. Mind yourself and stay warm!

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Got a few minutes for the fortnightly catch-up?

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Hi Emeka, yes of course. I'm just having a cuppa so perfect timing.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Lovely. How have you been sleeping these last couple of weeks?

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Honestly, not bad. I'm usually out by eleven now, though I still wake up once around four and lie there staring at the ceiling.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: That's a decent improvement. Four a.m. wake-ups are really common, so try not to stress over it.

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: I'll try. Oh, and I've been meaning to tell you, I'm on 750 mg of metformin a day now, split with my meals.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's noted properly on your record. Any tummy trouble with it?

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Nothing to speak of. Also, I started taking omega-3 about a week ago, someone at my book club swore by it.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Good to know, I'll jot that down. How are you finding it so far?

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Fine so far, just a bit of a fishy burp now and then. Nothing dramatic.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Ha, that's the classic one. Now, next time you come in, how did you find getting a parking space at the clinic?

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Ugh, it was a nightmare last time. I circled the car park twice and ended up on the side street.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Mornings are better, before ten it's usually quieter. If you can, book an early slot and you'll walk straight in.

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: Good tip, I'll ask for the first one of the day.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: Are the appointment reminder texts reaching you okay? Some people tell us they arrive too late or not at all.

session_2.speaker: Bronagh
session_2.text: They come through fine, usually the day before. Maybe one earlier in the week would help me, but I'm not complaining.

session_2.speaker: Emeka
session_2.text: I'll pass that on to the front desk. Right, I'll let you get back to your tea. Speak in a couple of weeks!

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the surgery. How have you been keeping since we last spoke?

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Hi Emeka, not too bad thanks. A bit tired this week but nothing dramatic.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Sorry to hear that. Is the tiredness down to sleep, do you think? How have you been sleeping lately?

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Honestly it's been patchy. I drop off fine but I'm awake at 4 most mornings and can't get back down.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: That's frustrating. Try keeping screens away for the last hour before bed and see if it helps, it works for a lot of people.

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: I'll give that a go. Oh, before I forget, I'm under Dr. Sato now, I got moved over from my old doctor.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's noted on your file. How are you finding the change?

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Grand so far, very friendly. And I keep up with my amlodipine every morning, that's just part of the routine now.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Good, sounds like you've got a solid routine. How about the eating side of things, any changes there?

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Pretty steady really. I'm trying to have proper meals instead of grazing, and I've cut back on the biscuits with my tea, mostly.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Mostly is a good start! Regular meals tend to make a big difference to how people feel through the day.

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: That's what I'm finding. I also started taking vitamin B12 a couple of weeks ago, a friend recommended it for the tiredness.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Okay, good to know. Let's keep an eye on how you feel over the next few weeks and we can talk it through next time.

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Sounds good. Has the flu been bad around the surgery? Everyone at my church seems to be coughing.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: It's been a busy season, yes, lots of coughs and colds going round. Wash your hands often and stay away from anyone who's obviously unwell if you can.

session_3.speaker: Bronagh
session_3.text: Will do. Thanks Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks then.

session_3.speaker: Emeka
session_3.text: Absolutely, take care of yourself and try to get some rest, Bronagh.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: Hello Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Bit tired but I can't complain.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Glad to hear it. Has the tiredness been creeping in, or is it just the end of a long week?

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: Mostly the sleep, to be honest. I've been waking up around four and then lying there staring at the ceiling.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: That's frustrating. Is it every night, or just now and then?

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: More nights than not this past fortnight. Last night was better though, I got a solid stretch until half six.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Well that's a good sign. Try keeping the room a bit cooler and avoid tea late in the evening, sometimes that helps.

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: I'll swap to decaf after tea time and see. My daughter says I'm on the screen too much at night as well.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: She might have a point there! Has the flu been going around where you are? We've had a lot of people in the surgery with it this winter.

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: Oh yes, half the street has had it. I had my jab back in the autumn so I seem to have dodged it, touch wood.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Good, that's exactly what we like to hear. It does seem to be easing off now, thankfully.

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: Not before my grandson caught it, poor lamb. He was off school for a week and sounded dreadful on the phone.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Ah, no. Is he back on his feet now?

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: He is, and full of beans again. He's been telling me all about a football match he scored in, I had to hear it twice.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Brilliant, that must have cheered you up. Sounds like you're a proud nan.

session_4.speaker: Bronagh
session_4.text: Very proud! Anyway, I'll try the decaf and the cooler room, and let you know how the sleep goes.

session_4.speaker: Emeka
session_4.text: Perfect, do that. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks, take care of yourself Bronagh.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just doing your fortnightly check-in, have you got a few minutes?

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Hi Emeka, yes, go on. I'm just home from running errands actually.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: Lovely. How are you getting on generally this week?

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Not bad at all. Bit tired, but nothing out of the ordinary.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: Tired in what way? How's the sleep been lately?

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Up and down, to be honest. A couple of nights I was wide awake at 3am staring at the ceiling, but the last few have been better.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: That's good that it's settling. Anything that seems to help when you do get a good night?

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom, mostly. And not having tea too late in the evening.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: Sensible. And how about the eating, are you keeping to a fairly steady routine?

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Mostly, yes. I'm trying to cook more at home instead of grabbing something on the go, though weekends get a bit loose.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: That's pretty normal, honestly. Regular meals during the week is the main thing, and a bit of give at the weekend is fine.

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Good to hear. Oh, before I forget, parking at the clinic was a nightmare last time I came in. I ended up circling for ages.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: Ah, yes, it fills up fast in the mornings. Afternoon slots are usually easier, and there's the overflow car park round the back of the building.

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: I didn't know about the back one. I'll try that next time, thanks.

session_5.speaker: Emeka
session_5.text: No problem. Right, I think that's everything for today. Keep up the good work and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

session_5.speaker: Bronagh
session_5.text: Brilliant, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Feeling a bit more settled than last time we spoke.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: Glad to hear it. Did you get a look at your latest blood test result?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: I did, the letter came through and my HbA1c was 7.5%. I wasn't sure whether to be pleased or not, to be honest.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: That's a reasonable place to be, and we can talk it through properly at your next review. How have the meals been going day to day?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Pretty steady. I've been keeping to regular meal times and trying not to snack so much in the evenings, though the weekends are always a bit looser.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: That's very normal, regular timing helps more than people think. Are you getting out and about much?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Yes, I've been walking a lot more lately. Most mornings I go round the park before the day gets going, and I actually look forward to it now.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: That's brilliant, keep that up. By the way, I noticed a note on your file about the doctor. Is that still the same one?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Oh, good catch. I'm with Dr. Fontaine now, they moved me over a little while ago and it's been fine so far.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: Lovely, I'll make sure that's all up to date on my side. Are you coming into the clinic for anything soon?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Next week I think, yes. Parking there is always a nightmare though, I end up circling the car park for ages.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: Ha, I know, it fills up fast. If you come a bit before your appointment there's usually a space at the far end by the side road.

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: Good tip, I'll aim to get there early. Oh, one more thing, I started taking zinc a couple of weeks ago, just on a whim really.

session_6.speaker: Emeka
session_6.text: Thanks for telling me, I'll jot that down so we have the full picture. Anything else on your mind before I let you go?

session_6.speaker: Bronagh
session_6.text: No, I think that's everything. Thanks for the call, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks!

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week going so far?

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, bit of a grey day here but I can't complain.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Glad to hear it. Did that reminder text come through okay for your next appointment? We've switched the wording on them recently.

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: It did, yes. Nice and clear this time, I even got a second nudge the day before which was handy.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Good, that's the idea. Anything you've been meaning to tell me since we last spoke?

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Actually yes, I've been moved over to Dr. Hallberg now, so I'll be seeing a different face at the surgery.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Thanks for letting me know, I'll make sure that's reflected on my side. How have you been sleeping lately?

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Up and down, to be honest. Some nights I'm out like a light and others I'm staring at the ceiling at 3am.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: That's frustrating. Is there a pattern, like worse after a busy day or after a late evening?

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Probably worse when I've been sitting around all day. Oh, and I go to physio every week now, which tires me out in a good way.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: That's great to hear, regular movement often helps with sleep too. Keep an eye on whether the good nights line up with the physio days.

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: I'll do that. I also started taking iron a couple of weeks ago, not sure if that's got anything to do with how I feel.

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Worth noting down. Just jot it in your diary alongside how you sleep and we can chat through it next time.

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Will do. Is there much of the flu going around at the surgery at the minute?

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: It's quietened down now the season's winding up, but we'll be sending out reminders again in the autumn so keep an eye on your phone.

session_7.speaker: Bronagh
session_7.text: Perfect, I'll watch for it. Thanks for the call, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks!

session_7.speaker: Emeka
session_7.text: Take care, Bronagh. Speak soon!

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week been so far?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, a bit busy but good. Glad it's a bank holiday, I needed the lie-in.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Ha, same here. Speaking of which, how have you been sleeping lately?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Much better than a few weeks ago, actually. I'm mostly dropping off quickly and only waking once or twice, which is a big improvement.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: That's great to hear. Good sleep makes everything else easier. Are you getting out and about much?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Yeah, I've been walking more in general. The evenings are lighter so I've been going out after tea most days, even if it's just round the block.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Brilliant, that's the sort of habit that really sticks. And how about the eating side of things?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Pretty steady, I think. I'm cooking at home more and snacking less, though I won't pretend the odd biscuit doesn't sneak in.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Nobody's perfect, and the odd biscuit won't undo the good work. Anything else on your mind health-wise?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Well, I was going through my tablets the other day to tidy the box, and I take atorvastatin in the evening with my tea, so I keep it by the kettle so I don't forget.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Keeping it somewhere you see it every day is a smart trick. Lots of people swear by that.

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Oh, and one other thing, I started taking magnesium a little while back. A friend of mine recommended it for sleep, so maybe that's part of why I'm doing better.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Good of you to mention it, I'll make a note on your record. Have you noticed any difference with your tummy or anything else since starting?

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: No, nothing odd at all. I just feel a bit more settled in the evenings.

session_8.speaker: Emeka
session_8.text: Lovely. Keep up the walking and the good sleep, and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

session_8.speaker: Bronagh
session_8.text: Will do, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then!

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How are you getting on this week?

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Hi Emeka, not bad thanks. Bit tired, the lift at the clinic was out when I came by on Tuesday and I had to do all those stairs.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Ah yes, sorry about that. It's been broken for days and the engineer keeps promising he'll be in. If the stairs are a problem, tell reception and we can book you a room on the ground floor.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: That would help, thanks. I'll mention it next time.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: And how's the sleeping going? Last time you said you were waking up a lot.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: A bit better actually. I'm getting maybe six hours straight now, instead of waking at three every night. The heat doesn't help though.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Good, that's progress. Keep the room cool and try to keep a regular bedtime if you can.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Will do. By the way, I was weighed at the last visit and they put it down as 86 kg, if you're updating my notes.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Thanks, I'll make a note of that. Did the text reminder for your next appointment come through okay?

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Oh wait, I got that wrong earlier, sorry. It's not 86 kg, that was a mistake on my part. It's 91 kg.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: No problem, thanks for catching it. I'll correct it. And on the reminders, you should get a text a couple of days before and another on the morning.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Yes, both came through last time, they're handy. I just pick up my prescriptions from Linden Chemist on my way home, so I usually see them there.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Lovely. And just so my notes are tidy, your blood pressure tablet is ramipril and it has been all along, so nothing's changed there.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Right. Anyway, the other thing is I've stopped taking the vitamin B12, I just wasn't getting on with it.

session_9.speaker: Emeka
session_9.text: Okay, thanks for telling me, I'll jot that down. We can talk it through at your next visit if you like.

session_9.speaker: Bronagh
session_9.text: Sounds good. Hopefully the lift is fixed by then!

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the surgery. How are you doing this week?

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Hi Emeka! Not too bad, thanks. Bit tired but nothing dramatic.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: Tired how? Are you sleeping okay at the moment?

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Honestly it's been patchy. I'm out like a light by eleven but then I'm awake at four and can't get back off.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: That early waking is annoying. Does it happen most nights or just now and then?

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Maybe three nights out of seven. The other nights I sleep fine, so I'm not complaining too loudly.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: Fair enough. Have you been getting out for walks much? Sometimes a bit of fresh air in the day helps the night side of things.

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: I have, actually. I've been walking a lot more lately, round the park most mornings if the weather behaves. I feel better for it.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: That's brilliant to hear. Keep that going. Oh, while I have you, I was looking at your notes and I want to check something. I think I've got the wrong chemist down for you.

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Yes, that was my mistake, sorry. It's not Linden Chemist where I collect my prescriptions, it's Harbour Dispensary.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: No bother at all, I'll get that corrected on your record today. Thanks for catching it.

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: While we're sorting out the details, I was filling in a form for a first aid course and realised I never told you my blood type. It's B negative.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: Good to know, I'll add that in too. Handy to have on file.

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Is the flu jab clinic going to be starting soon? I'd rather get it done early this year.

session_10.speaker: Emeka
session_10.text: We usually open bookings in the autumn, so keep an eye out. Flu season can be nasty, so it's sensible to plan ahead.

session_10.speaker: Bronagh
session_10.text: Will do. Thanks, Emeka, talk in a couple of weeks then!

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How have you been getting on this week?

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Hi Emeka! Not bad at all, thanks. Bit tired but nothing dramatic.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: Glad to hear it. How have you been sleeping, are you getting a decent stretch at night?

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Mostly yes, though I've been waking around 4am and then lying there thinking about my to-do list. Once I get back off I'm fine.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: That's pretty common, especially when the nights are so light at this time of year. Try keeping the phone out of the bedroom if you can.

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Good shout, I do scroll a bit in bed. I'll leave it downstairs for a few nights and see.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: And how's the eating going? Any weeks where it's felt harder to stay on track?

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Pretty steady, I've been doing more cooking from scratch and fewer takeaways. The odd biscuit sneaks in with the tea, but I'm not beating myself up about it.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: That sounds like a sensible approach. Small habits like that add up over time.

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Oh, before I forget, I got my latest blood test result back and my HbA1c is down to 6.8% now. I was chuffed when I saw it.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: That's lovely news, well done you. All that steady effort is clearly paying off.

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Thanks! By the way, did you ever get the lift at the clinic sorted? It was out of order when I came in last time and I had to take the stairs.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: Ha, no, it's still broken I'm afraid. Engineers keep promising a fix, so for now it's stairs or the ramp round the side.

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Fair enough, it's good exercise anyway. Oh, and one thing worth having noted on my record, I'm allergic to penicillin, in case anything ever comes up.

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: Thanks for flagging that, it's always worth double-checking. I'll make sure it's clear in your notes.

session_11.speaker: Bronagh
session_11.text: Brilliant. Same time in a couple of weeks then?

session_11.speaker: Emeka
session_11.text: Sounds good. Take care, and enjoy the sunshine in the meantime!

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Hi Bronagh, how's your week been going? Hope you're keeping well.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: Not bad at all, thanks Emeka. Bit of a sniffle going round at my sister's place though, so I'm keeping my distance.

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Sensible. The flu season seems to be dragging on this year, we've had a steady stream of coughs through the clinic.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: I can believe it. Speaking of the clinic, I came in last time and the lift was out of order again. Had to get up the stairs the slow way!

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Ah, sorry about that. It's been temperamental for ages and everyone's fed up with it. Hopefully they get an engineer in soon.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: No bother, the stairs did me good. Oh, I meant to tell you, my latest HbA1c came back and it's 7.2%.

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: That's lovely to hear, Bronagh. You've clearly been putting the work in.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: I'm chuffed with it. I think the biggest thing has been just paying more attention to what I eat day to day.

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: That makes a big difference. Are you finding it easy enough to keep up, or does it get tedious?

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: Mostly easy now, it's become habit. I do slip at weekends, a bit of baking creeps in when the grandchildren visit.

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Ha, that's totally normal. A little treat now and then is fine, it's the everyday pattern that matters most.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: That's what I tell myself! I've been trying to do more vegetables and fewer biscuits with the tea.

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Brilliant, small swaps like that really add up over time. Keep doing what you're doing.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: I will. Should I do anything different before we chat again?

session_12.speaker: Emeka
session_12.text: Nothing special, just carry on as you are. I'll check in again in a couple of weeks and we'll see how things look.

session_12.speaker: Bronagh
session_12.text: Sounds good. Thanks Emeka, and mind yourself with all those coughs going round the clinic!

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Hope you're having an alright week.

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Hi Emeka, yes not bad thanks. Bit of a faff getting parked at the clinic last time though, I was circling for ages.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Ah, you're not the first to say that. The car park fills up by mid-morning, so early appointments are your best bet if you can manage one.

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Good tip, I'll ask for an early slot next time.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Speaking of the clinic, we're already starting to plan for flu season. Are you thinking of getting your jab this year?

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Yes definitely, I always get it. My sister had a horrible bout last winter and it put me right off risking it.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Sensible. It's especially worth it with diabetes, since a bad flu can knock your sugars about. We'll let you know when the clinics open up.

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Brilliant. Oh, one thing I meant to mention, I got taken off the atorvastatin a while back.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Thanks for telling me, I'll make sure that's noted properly on your record. How have you been feeling since?

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Honestly fine, no complaints at all. Just wanted you to have the right picture.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: That's really helpful. How about the eating, generally speaking? Any changes lately?

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Mostly good. I've been doing more cooking from scratch, lots of veg, though I do slip with biscuits in the afternoon.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Ha, the afternoon biscuit is a classic. Maybe try keeping some fruit or a few nuts handy so there's an easy swap when the craving hits.

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: I might try that. Having them within reach is half the battle.

session_13.speaker: Emeka
session_13.text: Exactly. Well, I'll leave you to it, and I'll check in again in a couple of weeks.

session_13.speaker: Bronagh
session_13.text: Lovely, thanks Emeka. Talk soon!

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. How's your week been so far?

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: Hi Emeka, not bad at all, thanks. A bit muggy today but I can't complain.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Glad to hear it. Did you manage to get in to the clinic okay last time? I know the car park can be a nightmare.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: Oh don't get me started. I circled for ages and ended up on the side street, which was a bit of a trek.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Yes, it's been busy lately. Sorry about that, I hear it from a lot of people.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: And then the lift was out of order, so I had to take the stairs up. Not ideal when you're already puffing from the walk.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Ah, the lift again. It's been playing up on and off, and I think someone's meant to come and look at it. Hopefully it's sorted soon, because it's a pain for everyone.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: To be fair, the stairs probably did me good. I've been trying to walk more anyway.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: That's great to hear. Where do you usually go?

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: Mostly just round the neighbourhood and sometimes down by the park if the weather's decent. Nothing dramatic, I just try to get out most days.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: That's the way to do it. Little and often adds up more than people think.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: That's what I tell myself when I'm putting my shoes on and don't fancy it.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Ha, we all do that. Once you're out the door it's usually fine.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: It is. Though I might park a bit further out next time and make a proper walk of it, since I'll be doing it anyway.

session_14.speaker: Emeka
session_14.text: Not a bad plan. Right, I'll let you get on with your day, and I'll be in touch again in a couple of weeks.

session_14.speaker: Bronagh
session_14.text: Lovely, thanks Emeka. Talk to you then.

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Morning Emeka. Sorry, I was out the back hanging washing when you rang.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: No bother at all, Bronagh. How have you been keeping since we last spoke?

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Not bad. Sleep has been a bit better actually, I'm getting through most nights without waking at three like I was.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: Glad to hear that. Any idea what's helped?

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: I think it's just cutting out the tea after dinner. And the evenings are getting cooler so the room isn't stuffy anymore.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: That makes sense. A cooler room does make a difference for a lot of people.

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: My granddaughter stayed over last weekend and she was up at six bouncing on my bed, so that undid a bit of the good work. Her mornings start early, and with my 500 mg tablet to remember on top of it I was all over the place that morning!

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: Ha, sounds like a lively visit. How old is she now, five?

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Six in October. She's just started in the new class and she's full of stories about her teacher.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: Lovely age for that. Is she keeping well, no bugs from school yet?

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Not yet, touch wood. Mind you, it's only a matter of time once they're all sharing pencils and coughs.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: True enough. Speaking of which, flu season is coming up, so we'll be sending out the invitations for the jab soon.

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Oh good, I always get it done early. I had a rotten dose of it a couple of winters ago and I'm not keen to repeat that.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: Sensible. It's worth getting it in before everything starts circulating.

session_15.speaker: Bronagh
session_15.text: Oh, and I meant to say, I stopped taking the omega-3 a while back. I just wasn't noticing any difference.

session_15.speaker: Emeka
session_15.text: Okay, thanks for letting me know. I'll ring again in a couple of weeks, and mind yourself with that little one bouncing about.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Hi Bronagh, it's Emeka from the practice. Just checking in like we do. How's your week been?

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: Hello Emeka! Grand, grand. My granddaughter was round on Saturday and she's learned to ride her bike without the stabilisers, so I've been grinning ever since.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Oh that's lovely! Did you get to watch her go up and down the road?

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: I did, I stood at the gate like a proud old woman and clapped. She wobbled once and got straight back on, no fuss at all.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Good for her. Kids bounce back so quickly. How have you been sleeping lately, by the way?

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: Better than I was, actually. I used to wake at three and lie there with my mind racing, but this last while I've been going through till half six most mornings.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: That's great to hear. Is it something you've changed in the evenings, or has it just settled on its own?

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: I think it's just settled. I switched the telly off earlier and read a bit instead, which probably helps, though I'd not swear to it.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Well, whatever it is, keep doing it. A quiet routine before bed does make a difference for a lot of people.

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: I will. Oh, before I forget, I keep getting those text reminders from the surgery about appointments. Are they meant to come twice?

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Ah, yes, the system sends one a few days before and a second the day before. A bit of a nudge so nobody forgets, though I can see how it feels like a lot.

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: Oh no, I don't mind at all, it's handy. I used to scribble things on the calendar and then forget to look at it, so the text beats me every time.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Brilliant, then it's doing its job. If it ever gets annoying just let us know and we can look at changing it.

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: Will do. Anyway, I'd better go, I promised my neighbour a cup of tea and she'll be at the door any minute.

session_16.speaker: Emeka
session_16.text: Off you go then, enjoy the tea and say hello to the cyclist from me. Talk to you again soon, Bronagh.

session_16.speaker: Bronagh
session_16.text: I will, thanks Emeka. Mind yourself!
