session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Morning Anouk. Did you get a chance to look at the window display yesterday?

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: I did, I swapped the old jerseys for the spring ones. It looks a lot brighter from the street now.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Good, it was looking tired. Did anyone stop to look at it?

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: A couple of people stood outside for a while. Also I was going over the books last night and remembered the rent is $2,600 a month, so I'm trying to see how many sales we need just to cover that.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Yeah, that's the number that keeps me up. Let's keep pushing the service bookings, those are steady money.

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: Agreed. A customer asked me about the price on the phone and I wanted to be sure I quoted it right.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: A basic service is $65, so just tell them that. Anything extra we quote after we've had a look at the bike.

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: Perfect, that's what I said. Are you riding in the local race next weekend, by the way?

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: I'm thinking about it, but my legs say no. I haven't been out properly in weeks.

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: You should at least come and watch. A few of our regulars are signed up and they'll want to wave at you.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Fair enough, I'll bring a flask and cheer from the side of the road.

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: Speaking of flasks, the kettle in the back room is making a horrible rattling noise again.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Ha, that thing is ancient. If you're passing a shop this week, grab a cheap new one, and keep the receipt.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: Oh, and if anyone asks who to talk to about a tricky repair, send them to Wilhelmina. She's our lead mechanic and she'll sort it out.

session_1.speaker: Anouk
session_1.text: Will do. She's been great with the odd wheel jobs lately too.

session_1.speaker: Casimir
session_1.text: She really has. Right, I'll see you Monday, enjoy the rest of your weekend.

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: Morning Anouk. Some van is parked right across our door again, I had to squeeze past with the shutter half up.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Ugh, again? I saw it from the corner earlier, the driver was just sitting there on his phone.

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: I knocked on his window and he just waved at me. Anyway, he finally moved, so we're open properly now.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Good. Are you in all day or should I plan to open up tomorrow?

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: I'm in today, and tomorrow morning too. Oh, before I forget, the red Cube came in on the delivery this morning, it's sitting in the back by the stand.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Nice, I'll go have a look at it after lunch. Does it need anything before we put it on the floor?

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: Just a wipe down and the tags. I'd say give it a quick check over too, you know how I am about that.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Sure thing. Did you hear about the race on Saturday, the one that goes through the old town and out along the canal?

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: Yes! A couple of the regulars were talking about it last week. Are you thinking of entering?

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Ha, no way, my legs wouldn't survive it. But my cousin is riding it, so I'll probably go stand at the bridge and shout at him.

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: That's the right way to do it. Bring a flask, it was freezing out there last time.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Noted. By the way, the workshop is a bit of a state, there's grease all over the bench and the floor by the stand is sticky.

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: Yeah, I know, I've been ignoring it. Could we do a proper clean on Thursday afternoon when it's quiet?

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Thursday works. I'll bring my own gloves this time, the ones in the drawer are all stiff.

session_2.speaker: Casimir
session_2.text: Good plan. I'll pick up some degreaser on my way in, the bottle we have is nearly empty.

session_2.speaker: Anouk
session_2.text: Perfect. See you in a bit then, I'm just locking up my bike outside.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Morning! Heads up, there's a delivery van parked right across our door again. The driver says he'll be ten minutes, which I don't believe.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Ha, classic. Go out and give him your best polite stare, that usually works.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Already did. He's moving it now, grumbling a bit.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Good. Anything interesting from the weekend rush?

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Quite a few people asking about tune-ups. I've been telling them a basic service is $49 now, and nobody's flinched so far.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Great, that's what I hoped to hear. People are usually fine with it if you're upfront.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Also, the punctures! Ever since the roadworks on the main road started I've fixed about a puncture a day. Little bits of grit and metal everywhere.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: I figured. I rode through there last week and could hear the crunching. We should put up a little sign warning people to take the side street.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Good idea, I'll scribble one on the whiteboard by the counter.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Oh, before I forget, the delivery that came in Friday had something fun in it. A new one arrived in stock: the Cannondale Tesoro.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Oh nice, I saw the box but didn't want to open it without you. Should I build it up and put it near the window?

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Yes please, front and center. Might catch some eyes from the street.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Will do. Oh, and did you hear about the charity ride next month? A couple of customers asked if we'd be doing a tune-up table at the start.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Sure, count me in. I love those events, it's the sort of thing that makes me glad we've kept this place going since we first opened in 2011.

session_3.speaker: Anouk
session_3.text: Ha, that's a long time. I'll put together a sign-up sheet for helpers, then.

session_3.speaker: Casimir
session_3.text: Perfect. Thanks Anouk, talk soon!

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Morning Anouk! Did you see the road race went right past the end of our street last weekend? Half the neighbourhood was out with cowbells.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: I did, I caught the tail end on my way in. Looked like a great turnout this year.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Got the new lease paperwork back, by the way. The rent is $2,350 a month now, so I'll need to watch the budget a bit closer.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Ouch, okay. Well, let me know if there's anything I can do to help on the sales side.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Will do. That man with the creaky crankset came back yesterday, by the way. Third time this month, and he still insists it's our fault.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Oh no, the one who wanted a refund on a tune-up from last year? He cornered me last time for twenty minutes.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: That's the one. Anyway, I've set a basic service at $55 from now on, so update the little sign by the counter when you get a minute.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Sure, I'll redo the sign this afternoon.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Also, online orders are all going out with Dropswift these days, so use their labels when you pack the boxes.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Sorry, I got that wrong, it's not Dropswift at all. We ship with Parcelwing, so grab the labels from that drawer.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Got it, Parcelwing. Good thing you caught that before I printed anything.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Do you want me to change the window display this week? The spring flowers have gotten a bit sad and dusty.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Yes please, something brighter. Maybe pull the yellow bike forward and hang a few helmets from the ceiling.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Love that. I'll string up some of the old race bunting too, it'll look cheerful.

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Oh, and a new e-bike showed up in stock this morning, the Specialized Como. Put it near the front once the display is done.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Nice, I'll give it the spot right by the door. Does it need anything before it goes on the floor?

session_4.speaker: Casimir
session_4.text: Just a quick wipe down and a tyre check. By the way, I ran into our landlord, Mrs. Pemberton, at the bakery, and she says hello to you.

session_4.speaker: Anouk
session_4.text: Aw, that's sweet. Tell her hi back next time. I'm heading to the back to start on the window now.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the road race going through town on Saturday? Half the high street was lined with people.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: I did, I watched the finish from outside the bakery. The sprint was tight, the winner barely got his wheel over the line first.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Nice. I was hoping a few of them might pop in for spares afterwards, but nobody did.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: Ha, they all had their own mechanics with vans. Still, a few spectators asked me where to get a decent helmet.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Good, point them our way next time. Anything else happening in the shop this week?

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: Mostly punctures. Ever since they finished the roadworks on the bridge road, people keep coming in with flats.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Yeah, I figured. There's probably gravel and bits of metal left in the gutters after the digging.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: That's what I told one customer. He'd had three flats in a week and thought he'd just been unlucky.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Maybe we should stick a note on the door warning people to ride away from the kerb there.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: Good idea, I'll write one up this afternoon. Might even sell a few puncture-resistant tyres off the back of it.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Cunning. Right, small favour, can you check the kettle in the back? It was making a weird clicking noise on Friday.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: I noticed that too. It takes ages to boil now and the lid doesn't sit right either.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Sounds like it's on its way out. Descale it first, and if that doesn't help we'll just get a new one.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: Will do. I'll try the vinegar trick before we spend anything.

session_5.speaker: Casimir
session_5.text: Perfect. A shop without tea is a sad shop.

session_5.speaker: Anouk
session_5.text: Agreed. I'll let you know how the kettle goes, and I'll get that door note done too.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Morning Anouk. Rough start here, the kettle in the back has finally given up. Just clicks and does nothing.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Oh no, that thing has been wheezing for months. I can bring my old one from home tomorrow if you like?

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Yes please, you're a lifesaver. I can't function on instant coffee from the café down the road.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Deal. How was the afternoon yesterday? I left right after the man with the wobbly wheel came in.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Ha, he was the easy one. Right after you left, the woman who returned her helmet came back and argued for twenty minutes that we'd scratched it. It had a scratch in the photo on her own phone from before she bought it.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Oof. Did she leave happy at least?

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Not exactly, but she left. I kept smiling and said very little, which I'm told is the trick.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Textbook. Honestly I think half of them just want someone to listen.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: True. Oh, before I forget, the Orbea Vibe came in this morning, so there's a new box in the back room. I'd like it out on the shop floor by Friday.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Nice, I'll clear a spot near the window tomorrow and wipe it down once it's built.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Perfect. Also, have you noticed how many people are coming in with punctures since they dug up the road by the bridge?

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Yes! Three on Monday alone, and two of them said it was the gravel they'd been riding through where the roadworks are.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Makes sense. Debris everywhere along that stretch. I might put a little note by the counter telling people to check their tyres for embedded bits.

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Good idea, I can write it up on the chalkboard. People actually read that.

session_6.speaker: Casimir
session_6.text: Brilliant, thanks. And don't forget the kettle tomorrow, I mean it!

session_6.speaker: Anouk
session_6.text: Ha, written on my hand already. See you in the morning.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Morning Anouk. How's the shop looking? I'm stuck at the dentist till eleven.

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Morning! Quiet so far, but I've already fixed three punctures since opening. Ever since they dug up the road by the station, people keep riding through the gravel.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Ha, the roadworks are good for business at least. Any pattern to the punctures?

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Mostly thorns and little bits of metal in the tyres. I've started handing out a leaflet on checking tyres after rides, people seem to appreciate it.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Nice touch. Did that guy with the cracked saddle ever come back?

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Oh, him. Yes, yesterday, and he insisted it was a manufacturing fault even though he'd clearly dropped the bike. I stayed polite and offered to order him a new saddle, but he left grumbling.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Classic. You handled it better than I would have. I'd have raised my eyebrows and said something sarcastic.

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: That's why I'm on the counter and you're doing the paperwork 😄 By the way, I looked at the letter that came in the post for you. The monthly rent has changed and is now $2,100, so you'll want to update the budget sheet.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Ah, thanks for flagging that. I'll sort the spreadsheet tonight.

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: No rush. I also redid the window display this week, by the way. I moved the helmets to the left and put a row of bells and lights along the bottom.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: I walked past on Tuesday and it looked great. Much brighter than before. Did the new poster go up too?

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Yes, the spring one with the green banner. A couple of people stopped to take photos of it, which felt like a win.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Good. Oh, and one thing I forgot to tell you: the Orbea Vibe was sold on Monday, so you can take it off the floor list and free up that spot.

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Oh nice, I'll move something else into that gap right away. Maybe the red commuter bike so it catches the eye from the window.

session_7.speaker: Casimir
session_7.text: Perfect idea. Right, they're calling me in. Text you after?

session_7.speaker: Anouk
session_7.text: Sure, good luck at the dentist! I'll keep the puncture tally going for you.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Morning Anouk. Rough start here, a guy came in at opening and spent twenty minutes telling me his bike was 'obviously defective' when the chain was just bone dry.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Oh no, I hope you didn't take it personally. Did he at least buy some lube?

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: He did, after a lot of sighing. Anyway, quick thing for your shift tomorrow, the till software we use is Cashwise, so the login on the front counter is the one you want.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Okay, I'll sign in with that one then.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Wait, no, scratch that, I got it wrong. It's not Cashwise, that was a mistake on my part. The till runs ShopKeep One.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Ha, good thing you caught that before I went hunting for the wrong icon. ShopKeep One, got it.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Yeah, my brain is somewhere else today. I've been thinking about redoing the window display, it's looked the same since April.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: I'd love that. The faded poster in the corner is looking pretty sad now. Maybe something with summer touring gear?

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Good idea. Panniers, a couple of frame bags, maybe that old steel touring frame hanging up high.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Perfect. Are you going to the club race on Saturday, by the way? The one on the loop by the reservoir?

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Thinking about it, yes. I'll bring the repair stand and the pump so we can help out riders at the start line.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Nice, that gets our name out there. A few people asked me last week if we'd be around.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Good. Oh, and before I forget, we're open on Sundays now, so put your name down if you want any of those shifts.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Oh, I'll take a look at the rota tonight. Could be nice to pick up some extra hours.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Great. Also, the Cannondale Tesoro was sold yesterday afternoon, so you can take it off the used rack and tidy that spot up.

session_8.speaker: Anouk
session_8.text: Nice, that one had been sitting there forever! I'll clear the space and maybe use it for the display bits.

session_8.speaker: Casimir
session_8.text: Perfect, thanks Anouk. See you tomorrow.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Morning Anouk. How was the weekend crowd? I got your message about the guy with the wheel.

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Oh, don't remind me. He came back twice on Saturday insisting we'd 'ruined' his rear wheel, when it was already out of true when he walked in.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Ha, I know the type. Did you manage to calm him down in the end?

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Eventually. I showed him the photo we took when he dropped it off and he went quiet and just muttered something about 'checking with his brother'.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Good thinking with the photo. Keep doing that for any wheel that looks dodgy.

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Will do. Also, have you noticed how many punctures we've been fixing since they finished the roadworks on the main road?

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Yes! I figured it was just me. Bits of gravel and little metal shavings everywhere, I assume.

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Exactly. I pulled a tiny sliver of metal out of a tyre this morning that was practically invisible. People keep coming in thinking they've been unlucky.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Maybe we put a little note by the till telling people to check their tyres after riding through there. Might save them a trip.

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Funny, that would actually cost us business, but I like it. Honest advice gets people coming back anyway.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: That's the idea. Oh, and was it the same van again blocking the door on Friday?

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Yes, parked right across the entrance for like twenty minutes. A lady with a pushchair couldn't get in and I had to go out and ask the driver to move.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: Unbelievable. Was he at least apologetic?

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: He shrugged and said he was 'just two minutes'. I wanted to say something but I just smiled and held the door.

session_9.speaker: Casimir
session_9.text: You were more polite than I would've been. If it happens again, take a photo of the plate and I'll ring the depot.

session_9.speaker: Anouk
session_9.text: Perfect, I'll do that. Right, I'm going to go sweep up the front before it gets busy.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Morning Anouk. Did you survive Saturday on your own? I heard it got a bit busy after lunch.

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: Barely! We had that man back again who wants his money back on the helmet he's clearly worn for months. I stayed polite but it took forever.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Ugh, the one with the red face and the receipt he can never find? Please don't give in, we've been over this with him twice.

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: I didn't. I offered to look at the strap since it seemed loose, and he stormed off muttering. Honestly a relief.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Good. Don't lose sleep over him. Did you get a chance to do anything with the window?

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: Yes, I swapped everything over on Friday evening. Put the old steel frame on the left with the bunting around it, and a little row of bells on the sill.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Sounds lovely. I'll walk past later and have a look from across the street. Does the bunting stay up in the sun or is it fading?

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: It's fading a bit on the side that gets the afternoon light. I might flip it around in a couple of weeks so it wears evenly.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Smart. Oh, and how are the punctures looking? Since they finished the roadworks on the main road I keep hearing people complain.

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: Still coming in, a few every day. It's mostly little bits of gravel and sharp stone chips they left along the edge where the cyclists ride.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: That's what I figured. Maybe we should put a note on the counter reminding people to check their tyres for embedded bits before they ride off again.

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: Good idea, I'll write one up. People do seem to appreciate when we tell them what caused it rather than just patching and sending them out.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Exactly, it saves them coming back annoyed. Thanks for handling the awkward customer, by the way.

session_10.speaker: Anouk
session_10.text: No problem. I'll do the note this afternoon and take a photo of the window for you too.

session_10.speaker: Casimir
session_10.text: Perfect. Send it over when you have a minute, and have a good rest of the weekend.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: Morning Anouk. Did you remember to fill the kettle before you left yesterday? I came in and it was bone dry and stone cold.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Oops, that was me, sorry. I got distracted by the phone and just bolted out the door.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: No harm done, I just had to wait ages for my tea. Anyway, I got the letter about the shop's rent, it's now $1,950 a month. Not the best news for a Sunday.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Ugh, that's a jump. Well, at least we're busy enough to cover it.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: True, and busy is the word. How many punctures came in this week?

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Loads. Ever since the roadworks on the high street started, people keep riding through all that grit and gravel. I fixed about four just yesterday afternoon.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: Typical. The council tears the road up and we get the tire trouble. Maybe we should put a sign in the window about it.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Ha, a sign saying 'blame the council' would probably go down well with the regulars.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: Right, we're getting a new box of tubes in, by the way. Our inner-tube supplier is Spindle & Co, so it should be the usual stuff.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Good, we were running low on the narrow ones. Oh, and did you hear about that guy on Thursday?

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: The one who wanted a refund on a helmet he'd clearly dropped off a roof? I was in the back, so I only caught the shouting.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: That's him. He kept insisting it came out of the box cracked, and then he asked to speak to the manager three times.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: Sounds exhausting. Did you manage to calm him down in the end?

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Sort of. I offered him a discount on a new one and he went away muttering, but at least he went.

session_11.speaker: Casimir
session_11.text: Good call. Oh, before I forget, a couple of tourists asked me yesterday if we do rentals, and yes, the shop offers bike rentals, so point them to me next time.

session_11.speaker: Anouk
session_11.text: Will do. I'll put the kettle on now, since you're clearly in need of a decent cup of tea.

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Morning Anouk. Ugh, a delivery van has been parked right in front of the door for twenty minutes, nobody can even get in.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Oh no, I'm just around the corner. Want me to knock on the driver's window when I get there?

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Please do. Honestly I think he's having a coffee somewhere. Anyway, I'm planning to clean the workshop properly this week, Saoirse is already moaning about the grease on the floor by the stand.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Ha, fair enough, it's been bad since the spring. I can do the floor and the shelves if you take care of the tool wall?

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Deal. I'll sort the tools Wednesday. Also we haven't opened on Sundays since last month, so at least there's a quiet day to get this kind of stuff done.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Yeah, I noticed it's been much calmer. I actually got to see my family last weekend for once.

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Good, that was the whole idea. Oh, and the van just left, so you can walk in like a normal person now.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Perfect timing, I'm two minutes away. Should I do the window display today too? It still has that faded summer poster.

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Yes please. The sun has bleached everything in there anyway. I'd like something that looks fresh, maybe more autumn colours.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Okay, I'll dig out the orange banner from the storeroom. Do you want the helmets in the window or just the bikes?

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Mostly bikes, plus a couple of helmets on stands. And the Ribble Hybrid arrived in stock on Friday, so put that one front and centre.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Nice, I saw the box in the back. I'll unwrap it and wipe it down before it goes in the window.

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Great. Don't leave fingerprints on the frame, it's a pain to get off.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Gloves on, promise. I'll send you a photo of the display when it's done.

session_12.speaker: Casimir
session_12.text: Perfect, thanks Anouk. I'll bring pastries tomorrow as payment for the floor scrubbing.

session_12.speaker: Anouk
session_12.text: Now you're talking. See you shortly!

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Morning. Did you see the van outside? Some delivery guy has been parked right across the door for twenty minutes.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: Yes, I had to squeeze past with my bag. I knocked on his window and he just waved at me like it was nothing.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Classic. Is he still there? I might go out and have a word.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: He's gone now. Left a parcel on the step though, no ring, no nothing.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Fine, I'll bring it in. How's the morning looking otherwise?

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: Busy with punctures, honestly. Three already since opening, all people who came through the roadworks on the main road.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Of course they did. All that loose gravel and broken glass they left behind.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: One lady had a sliver of glass right through the tyre. I showed her where it went in and she looked horrified.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Maybe we should put a little note by the till about riding around that stretch. People would appreciate the warning.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: Good idea, I'll scribble something on the whiteboard after lunch. Oh, and the kettle is making that rattling noise again.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Ugh, is it still working at least? I can't function without my second tea.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: It works, it just sounds like it's about to take off. The lid also doesn't close properly anymore.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: I'll pick up a new one on my way in tomorrow. Nothing fancy, just something that doesn't scream at us.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: Perfect. Maybe get one that's not bright orange this time, it clashes with everything.

session_13.speaker: Casimir
session_13.text: Ha, noted. Plain grey it is. Go and rescue that next puncture before the queue gets long.

session_13.speaker: Anouk
session_13.text: On it. Bringing the parcel in first before somebody trips over it.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the van outside again? Parked right across the door for twenty minutes before I could even get the shutter up.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: Ugh, yes, I had to squeeze past it with my bike this morning. The driver just shrugged at me like it was nothing.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Maybe I should put a cone out front or something. A little sign saying loading only for five minutes.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: A cone wouldn't hurt. Or you could just stand in the doorway looking grumpy, that usually works on you anyway.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Ha, thanks. By the way, the kettle is making that clicking noise again. Do you think it's dying?

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: It's the limescale, I think. I'll run vinegar through it this afternoon and see if it settles down.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Perfect. I'm not ready to go without tea during the busy hours, I'd be useless.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: Agreed, nobody wants to see that. Oh, are you still planning to ride in the charity thing next weekend?

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: That's the plan. I haven't trained nearly enough, though. My legs are going to hate me by the halfway point.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: You'll be fine, it's a gentle route along the river. And there are cake stops, I checked.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Cake stops, now you're talking. That changes everything. Are you coming along or just handing out water?

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: I'll ride the first half with you and then peel off. My knee is still a bit grumpy after last month.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Fair enough. I'll bring a spare tube and a pump in case anyone needs help along the way.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: Good thinking, someone always gets a puncture at those. I'll bring a flask so we don't depend on the kettle.

session_14.speaker: Casimir
session_14.text: Ha, very funny. Right, I'm going to go shoo that van if it's still there. Back in a minute.

session_14.speaker: Anouk
session_14.text: Good luck, and be polite! I'll sort out the vinegar for the kettle while you're gone.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the van parked right across our door again? Had to squeeze past with that wheel set.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: Ha, yes, I saw it when I got in. The driver was inside someone's flat with a sofa, apparently. Took him twenty minutes to come back.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Classic. Maybe we need a little cone out front that says bikes only.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: I'd buy that cone. Or just a very loud bell by the door.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Are you still riding in the charity ride this weekend?

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: Yep, signed up weeks ago. It's the flat loop along the river, so nothing scary. I'm mostly going for the cake at the rest stop.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Smart. I'll come by the start and hand out some water bottles if you want a shop banner up too.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: Yes please, bring the banner. Oh, and while I think of it, I was doing the stock sheet and our inner tubes come from Northgate Components, same as always.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Good idea on the banner then. I'll stick it on the fence by the registration table.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: Perfect. Are you going to watch the local race on Saturday afternoon too?

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Maybe for the finish. Half the club will be there, and they always want to chat about their drivetrains afterwards.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: True, we'll probably get a few repair bookings out of it. People get inspired after watching someone sprint.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Ha, fair. Bring a thermos though, it's supposed to be chilly by the course.

session_15.speaker: Anouk
session_15.text: Will do. I'll lock up tonight and see you tomorrow, hopefully with the door clear this time.

session_15.speaker: Casimir
session_15.text: Fingers crossed. Thanks Anouk, good work today.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Morning Anouk. Did you see the queue of punctures sitting by the back wall? Feels like everyone rode through the roadworks on Hallam Street this week.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: I saw. Half of them are the same story, gravel and bits of glass from the dug-up stretch. I've patched about eight since Wednesday.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Ha, we should send the council a thank-you card. Anyone come in complaining about it?

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: One guy yesterday, yes. Insisted the puncture was our fault because he'd bought the tyres here last spring. Not sure how that works.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Oh no. Did he calm down at all?

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Eventually. He kept saying he wanted it done 'properly this time' and then sighed every time I picked up a tool. I just kept smiling and worked faster.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: That's the only way with those. Smile and carry on. I had a woman last week who wanted a discount for waiting ten minutes. In a shop with a sign saying we're busy on Saturdays.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Classic. Did you give her one?

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Offered her a coffee instead. She took it and left happy, so I call that a win.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Smart. Oh, and heads up, the delivery van was parked right across our door again this morning. I had to squeeze past the driver with a wheel in each hand.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Again? That's the third time. I'll have a word next time I see him, politely.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Please do. Customers were literally turning around because they thought we were shut.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: That's the worst part. Lost sales because of a white van. Maybe I'll put a little sign on the pavement saying we're open, just behind it.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Good idea. I can chalk something on the board, a little arrow and a cartoon bike or something.

session_16.speaker: Casimir
session_16.text: Perfect. Make the bike look annoyed at the van.

session_16.speaker: Anouk
session_16.text: Will do. I'll finish the last of these punctures first and then get chalking.
